classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient for down-gradient diffusion of neutral momentum along
the toroidal direction, resolved for one electronic, vibrational, or
rotational internal state.
items.documentation:
This coefficient governs diffusive transport of [momentum](name:momentum)
along the toroidal direction for a selected neutral species in one specified
internal state. The toroidal direction follows increasing toroidal angle in
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a local, componentwise Fick-law closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{0a,\phi} = -D_{0a,\phi}\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial g_{0a}}{\partial\phi}
$$

where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{0a,\phi}$ is the toroidally directed diffusive
flux of a selected momentum component, $D_{0a,\phi}$ is this diffusion
coefficient, and $g_{0a}$ is the corresponding momentum density. The
subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $a$ identifies their internal
state. The derivative is taken at fixed major radius and vertical height;
the geometric factor converts the angular derivative to a derivative along
physical toroidal arc length.

The coefficient applies to the specified internal state, without summation
or averaging over other internal states. The toroidal qualifier selects the
flux and gradient direction, not the transported momentum component. This
momentum-density-gradient closure excludes convective transport,
nondiffusive momentum flux, and momentum sources; it is not defined by a
flow-velocity gradient.

This quantity is the toroidal directional member of the [neutral
internal-state momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient).
The corresponding [poloidal
member](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead selects the poloidal transport direction.

items.name: radial_total_momentum_source
items.description:
Signed rate of momentum input or removal per unit area in the major-radius
direction, summed over all included particle populations.
items.documentation:
The radial total momentum source is the major-radius component of the net
momentum-transfer rate per unit area supplied to or removed from all
included particle populations. It is a directional projection of the [total
momentum source](name:total_momentum_source), not a coordinate locating the
momentum.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, this
projection is defined by:

$$
S_R = \mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{tot}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $S_R$ is the radial total momentum source, $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{tot}}$
is the total momentum-source vector, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward
increasing distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.

The total is the algebraic sum of contributions from all included particle
populations, not a sum of their magnitudes. The source is area-normalized
rather than a volumetric force density. The major-radius direction is not
generally normal to a magnetic flux surface; the [toroidal momentum
source](name:toroidal_momentum_source) instead resolves momentum transfer
along the toroidal direction.

This quantity describes gain or loss of [momentum](name:momentum) through
source processes. It is distinct from [total momentum
flux](name:total_momentum_flux), which describes momentum transported across
an oriented surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the net source adds momentum in the direction
of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: normalized_plasma_internal_inductance
items.description:
Normalized internal inductance measures internal poloidal magnetic energy
relative to squared plasma current and the plasma's geometric-axis major
radius.
items.documentation:
Normalized internal inductance measures the poloidal magnetic energy
contained within the entire plasma using the geometric-axis normalization
known as li(3). It characterizes poloidal-field peaking associated with the
plasma current distribution.

The normalized internal inductance $l_i$ is defined by

$$
l_i = \frac{2\int_V B_{\mathrm{p}}^2\,dV}{\mu_0^2 I_{\mathrm{p}}^2 R_{\mathrm{geo}}}
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude, $V$ is the
plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mu_0$ is the vacuum permeability,
$I_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the total toroidal plasma current, and
$R_{\mathrm{geo}}$ is the major radius of the plasma's geometric axis.

The integral covers the full plasma volume and excludes magnetic energy
outside the plasma and energy associated with the toroidal magnetic field.
The normalization requires nonzero plasma current and uses the geometric
axis rather than the magnetic axis.

The corresponding dimensional internal inductance $L_i$ satisfies $L_i =
\mu_0 R_{\mathrm{geo}}l_i/2$. This normalization distinguishes the quantity
from dimensional [plasma inductance](name:plasma_inductance).

items.name: parallel_wave_magnetic_field
items.description:
Signed component of the oscillatory electromagnetic-wave magnetic
perturbation along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction, distinct
from the total parallel magnetic field.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the field-aligned component of the oscillatory magnetic
perturbation carried by a coherent electromagnetic wave. It excludes
equilibrium and other static magnetic-field contributions.

The component is defined by

$$
B_{\rm parallel}^{\rm wave} = \delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq}
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_{\rm wave}$ is the wave magnetic-field perturbation
and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_{\rm eq} = \mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}/|\mathbf{B}_{\rm eq}|$
is the local unit vector along the equilibrium magnetic field. It is a
component of the parent wave magnetic field, not its magnitude or a
complex-quadrature part. Unlike [parallel magnetic
field](name:parallel_magnetic_field), it does not include the equilibrium
field.

Sign convention: Positive when the wave magnetic-field perturbation points
in the direction of the local equilibrium magnetic-field unit vector.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical decay of
ordered toroidal flow momentum carried by ions of one specified species and
charge state.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate quantifies relaxation of
the toroidal component of ordered [momentum](name:momentum) through
collisional friction and neoclassical viscous stresses. It applies to ions
of one specified species and charge state. The toroidal direction follows
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local linear relaxation closure, the damping contribution to the
momentum balance is:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial \delta g_{s,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\phi}\,\delta g_{s,\phi}
$$

where $\nu_{s,\phi}$ is this damping rate, $\delta g_{s,\phi}$ is the
departure of the ordered toroidal momentum density from its relaxation
equilibrium, $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, and $t$ is
time. The restriction labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ isolates the damping
contribution rather than the complete momentum balance. For damping, the
coefficient is nonnegative regardless of the direction of the momentum
departure.

This coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
charge states, and is distinct from the species-level [toroidal ion momentum
damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate). It excludes momentum
diffusion, convection, and external momentum injection. Momentum transferred
out of this charge state need not represent a loss of total plasma momentum.

It is the toroidal directional entry of the [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate), whereas the
[poloidal ion charge-state momentum damping
rate](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) governs
relaxation of the poloidal momentum component.

items.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Toroidal helium-4 velocity at the magnetic axis is the signed bulk-flow
velocity of helium-4 ions projected onto the toroidal φ direction of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame at the magnetic axis.
items.documentation:
Toroidal helium-4 velocity at the magnetic axis is the signed bulk-flow
velocity of helium-4 ions projected onto the toroidal basis vector of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame at the magnetic axis. As a
species-level velocity, it is the density-weighted mean over all charge
states of helium-4 present at that locus.

The scalar projection is defined by:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the density-weighted
mean helium-4 bulk-flow velocity vector at the magnetic axis and
$\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is localized to the magnetic axis and is distinct from the
corresponding [toroidal helium-4 velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). It is
species-specific to helium-4 and is distinct from [toroidal helium-3
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

items.name: toroidal_angle_of_aperture
items.description:
Toroidal angular coordinate locating the geometric center of a collimating
aperture around the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal angular coordinate $\phi_c$ of an aperture's
reference center, locating that center around the machine symmetry axis.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Using the right-handed
Cartesian basis $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$, with $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{y}$ as
horizontal unit vectors and $\hat{z}$ aligned with the vertical cylindrical
direction $\hat{Z}$, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
\phi_c = \operatorname{atan2}(Y_c, X_c)
$$

Here, $\phi_c$ is the toroidal angle of the aperture center, $X_c$ and $Y_c$
are its horizontal Cartesian coordinate values along $\hat{x}$ and
$\hat{y}$, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ is the two-argument azimuth function
referenced to the chosen $\phi=0$ direction.

The quantity applies to one aperture reference center. For a circular
aperture, this reference is the circle's geometric center; for an aperture
represented by a local plane, it is the origin of the local coordinate
system located within the aperture area. It is not the toroidal angle of an
arbitrary aperture point, the aperture orientation, the beam direction, or
an aggregate over multiple apertures.

This coordinate is the toroidal counterpart of the [vertical coordinate of
an aperture](name:vertical_coordinate_of_aperture), which gives the $Z$
location of the same center. The equivalent center-based convention is also
represented by [toroidal coordinate of an
aperture](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_aperture); neither coordinate
specifies the aperture's radial location, size, or orientation.

Sign convention: Positive when the aperture center lies in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ from the chosen $\phi=0$ reference.

items.name: neutral_species_density
items.description:
Particle number density of a designated neutral species, counting its
neutral particles per physical volume.
items.documentation:
The density of a specified neutral species is the local population of
neutral particles of that species per physical volume. It is resolved by
species rather than representing a combined density of different neutral
species.

$$
n_N = \frac{dN_N}{dV}
$$

where $n_N$ is the neutral-species number density, $N_N$ is the number of
neutral particles of the designated species, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity applies only to the neutral form of the designated species;
ions and other neutral species are excluded. Its aggregation is over neutral
particles of that one species, without implying a sum over species or a
particular population subdivision.

[volume_averaged_neutral_species_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density)
is a volume-averaged specialization of this quantity over the plasma volume
enclosed by the last closed flux surface during plasma initiation.

items.name: plasma_filament_width
items.description:
Full horizontal extent of the rectangular cross-section of a discrete plasma
current-carrying filament element, measured along the major-radius direction
in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Full horizontal extent of the rectangular cross-section of a discrete plasma
current-carrying filament element, measured along the major-radius direction
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is the side length
of the idealized rectangular filament cross-section parallel to the $R$
coordinate, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a rectangular cross-section bounded by minimum and maximum major-radius
coordinates, the width $w$ is defined by:

$$
w = R_{\max} - R_{\min}
$$

where $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$ are the lower and upper major-radius
coordinates of the rectangle boundary.

This quantity is a non-negative geometric extent: $w \ge 0$ and $R_{\max}
\ge R_{\min}$ are part of the definition. It is not a signed displacement, a
coordinate position, or the [current](name:current_of_plasma_filament)
assigned to the filament; it is distinct from the
[height](name:height_of_plasma_filament), the vertical extent along $Z$, and
from the thickness, a separate filament cross-section extent.

items.name: maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Maximum allowed value of the signed rotation angle of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror within its mechanical travel range.
items.documentation:
The upper mechanical travel limit is the greatest permitted value of the
mirror’s signed rotation angle, bounding the accessible steering range of
the launcher. It is a limit of the mechanical actuator, not the mirror angle
during a particular operating condition.

Let $\theta$ denote the signed mirror angle defined by angle of
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. The upper limit $\theta_{\max}$ is
defined by

$$
\theta_{\max} = \sup\{\theta \mid \theta\text{ is mechanically accessible}\}
$$

The quantity excludes the lower travel limit and does not describe the
mirror’s position unless that position equals the upper boundary of the
allowed range.

Sign convention: Positive when the mirror rotates in the positive sense
defined for angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror.

items.name: poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
items.description:
Poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed poloidal projection
of the neoclassical return current that compensates divergent
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current in toroidal magnetic geometry.
items.documentation:
Poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density is the signed projection of the
[Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) onto the local poloidal
tangent. This return-current contribution restores local current continuity
where the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current is divergent in toroidal
magnetic geometry.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm p}=\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\mathbf j_{\mathrm{PS}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm p}$ is the poloidal Pfirsch–Schlüter current density,
$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the parent Pfirsch–Schlüter current-density
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the oriented poloidal unit
tangent. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The poloidal
tangent lies within a plane of constant $\phi$ and is tangent to the
magnetic flux surface. Its orientation follows increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$, whose orientation must be specified by the poloidal-angle
convention.

This quantity is the local net Pfirsch–Schlüter contribution from the
included plasma charge carriers, without species or charge-state resolution.
It is a mechanism-specific component of [current
density](name:current_density), not the total plasma current density, the
parent vector's magnitude, or a flux-surface average; no restriction to the
edge plasma is implied.

The [parallel Pfirsch–Schlüter current
density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density) projects the same
parent vector onto the magnetic-field direction instead. Its projection
direction is therefore distinct from the geometric poloidal tangent.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional positive charge flows in the
direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: y_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone
items.description:
The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an
elliptic shatter cone is its projection in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y,
z) frame.
items.documentation:
The signed y component of the unit vector along the major axis of an
elliptic shatter cone is the projection of that major-axis direction onto
the $y$ basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y},
\hat{z})$ frame. The major-axis direction is the orientation of the
principal semiaxis of the cone's elliptic cross-section.

The component is defined by

$$
e_{\mathrm{maj},y} = \hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot \hat{y}
$$

where $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ is the y component of the shatter-cone major-axis
unit vector, $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ is the unit vector along the major
axis of the elliptic shatter cone, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of
the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity applies to the geometry of an elliptic shatter cone and to the
major semiaxis orientation of its elliptic cross-section; its aggregation
convention is none, because it is a single vector component rather than a
sum or mean. It is distinct from the unsigned major-axis length, from the [y
component of the shatter-cone direction unit
vector](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which describes the
cone direction rather than the major-axis orientation, and from the [y
component of the minor-axis unit
vector](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), which refers to the
orthogonal minor semiaxis.

Together with the [x
component](name:x_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) and [z
component](name:z_major_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), this quantity
forms the Cartesian representation of $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$; the linked x
and z components and $e_{\mathrm{maj},y}$ satisfy $(e_{\mathrm{maj},x})^2 +
(e_{\mathrm{maj},y})^2 + (e_{\mathrm{maj},z})^2 = 1$, where
$e_{\mathrm{maj},x}$ and $e_{\mathrm{maj},z}$ are the linked x and z
components. The major-axis and minor-axis unit vectors jointly orient the
elliptic cone and satisfy $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}} \cdot
\hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}} = 0$, where $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{min}}$ is the
minor-axis unit vector with
[x](name:x_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone),
[y](name:y_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone), and
[z](name:z_minor_axis_unit_vector_of_shatter_cone) components.

Sign convention: Positive when $\hat{e}_{\mathrm{maj}}$ has a component in
the $+\hat{y}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y},
\hat{z})$ frame.

items.name: radial_outline_of_limiter_tile
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate R locating each point on the boundary outline of a
plasma-facing limiter tile in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial outline coordinate is the major-radius value $R$ of each point on
the geometric boundary outline of a plasma-facing limiter tile. It describes
tile geometry rather than a plasma field or a flux-surface coordinate.

In a right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius
coordinate is defined from Cartesian coordinates by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, and
$x$ and $y$ are Cartesian coordinate values along the $\hat{x}$ and
$\hat{y}$ axes of the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis.

The quantity is evaluated pointwise for every contour point of the
limiter-tile outline. It is not an average, maximum, area, or integrated
boundary measure; for a closed contour, the first point is not repeated at
the end.

Together with the [vertical outline of the limiter
tile](name:vertical_outline_of_limiter_tile), it supplies the complementary
radial and vertical coordinates that locate the outline in a poloidal
cross-section. The related [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate)
expresses the same geometric coordinate concept without specifying the
limiter-tile outline locus.

items.name: parallel_neutral_particle_flux
items.description:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the signed net number flow of one neutral
species along the local magnetic field per unit perpendicular area and time,
summed over internal states.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral particle flux is the local signed net number flow of one
neutral atomic or molecular species along the magnetic-field direction, per
area perpendicular to that direction. Particle crossings in opposite
directions contribute with opposite signs.

The parallel projection is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\parallel}$ is the parallel neutral particle flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$ is the particle number-flux vector of the selected
neutral species, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and
$|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The subscript $0$ identifies neutral
particles. This projection requires a nonzero magnetic field.

The quantity is summed over all internal states of the selected species, not
over different neutral species. The [parallel neutral internal-state
particle flux](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux) resolves
the individual state contributions whose sum gives this quantity.

This is the specialization of [neutral particle
flux](name:neutral_particle_flux) for a crossing surface whose normal
follows the local magnetic-field direction. It is not a flux per actual
material-surface area at an arbitrary field-incidence angle, a
surface-integrated arrival rate, or a one-way incident flux. The magnetic
field defines the projection direction without implying that neutral
trajectories follow magnetic field lines.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral particle transport points
along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: tilt_angle_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Signed inclination of a passive conducting loop element’s overall geometric
reference axis in the poloidal plane, distinct from oblique cross-section
shape angles.
items.documentation:
The tilt angle specifies the orientation of a passive conducting loop
element’s directed geometric reference axis in the poloidal plane. It
describes the overall orientation of the element, not an inclination
parameter defining the shape of an oblique cross-section, and is analogous
to the orientation defined for a [tilt angle of a plasma
filament](name:tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament).

Let the reference-axis direction have components $t_R$ and $t_Z$ along the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and
$Z$ is vertical height. The tilt angle is defined by

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{tilt}} = \operatorname{atan2}(t_Z,t_R)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the directed angle from the outward
$+R$ direction toward the upward $+Z$ direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the reference axis rotates from $+R$ toward
$+Z$.

items.name: toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of beryllium ions at the
internal transport barrier, combining all beryllium ionization states.
items.documentation:
The toroidal beryllium velocity at the internal transport barrier is the
bulk-flow component of the beryllium ion population evaluated at the radial
position of the barrier. It combines all beryllium ionization states and
excludes neutral beryllium.

The charge-state-averaged velocity is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be}} = \frac{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z} v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}}{\sum_Z n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}}
$$

where $Z$ is beryllium charge state, $n_{\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its ion number
density, and $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Be},Z}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component.
It is the internal-transport-barrier counterpart of [toroidal beryllium
velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and [toroidal
beryllium velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_beryllium_velocity_at_pedestal_top).

Sign convention: Positive when the beryllium-ion flow is in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: fluctuating_saturated_ion_current_density
items.description:
Temporal standard deviation of the ion charge flux per collecting area at a
Langmuir-probe collector biased into ion saturation, with electron
collection suppressed.
items.documentation:
The fluctuating saturated ion current density is the temporal standard
deviation of [saturated ion current
density](name:saturated_ion_current_density). It describes the amplitude of
boundary-plasma ion-collection fluctuations, not the mean saturation level.

The fluctuation amplitude is defined by:

$$
\sigma_{j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}} = \sqrt{\left\langle\left(j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}(t)-\left\langle j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}\right\rangle_t\right)^2\right\rangle_t}
$$

where $\sigma_{j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}}$ is the temporal standard deviation,
$j_{i,\mathrm{sat}}(t)$ is the collected ion saturation current density at
time $t$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_t$ denotes temporal averaging over the
same specified interval at one collector. The subscript $i$ denotes ions and
$\mathrm{sat}$ denotes the ion-saturation regime.

The collector is sufficiently negatively biased relative to the local plasma
to suppress electron collection. The underlying ion signal includes the
charge-weighted contributions of all collected ion species and charge
states; the standard deviation is taken after those contributions are
combined, rather than summed from their separate standard deviations.
Electron-current fluctuations are excluded, and the averaging is temporal
rather than spatial.

This is a fluctuation statistic of collector-defined [current
density](name:current_density), not an instantaneous signed perturbation or
an uncertainty in the temporal mean. Unlike [parallel fluctuating ion
current density](name:parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density), it refers
to ion-saturation collection rather than projection onto the local
magnetic-field direction.

items.name: coolant_transit_time_of_plant_component_port
items.description:
Elapsed time for coolant to traverse the associated plant component from
inlet to outlet, defining the thermal delay between the two coolant states.
items.documentation:
Coolant transit time is the elapsed travel time for the coolant stream to
pass through the plant component associated with the specified port, from
its inlet to its outlet. It represents the transport delay between the inlet
and outlet thermal states.

The transit time is defined as

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{c}} = t_{\mathrm{out}} - t_{\mathrm{in}}
$$

where $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$ is the coolant transit time, $t_{\mathrm{in}}$ is
the instant when the coolant crosses the component inlet, and
$t_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the instant when the same coolant stream crosses the
component outlet.

The quantity applies to the coolant path through one associated plant
component and uses the inlet-to-outlet interval as its aggregation
convention. It is not a plant-wide sum over components or ports, and it
excludes transport outside the component, instrumentation or network
latency, and a thermal time constant of the component material.

The transit time establishes the temporal correspondence between inlet
conditions and the delayed outlet state represented by the [coolant
temperature at outlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_outlet). It is distinct
from the [coolant mass flow rate](name:coolant_mass_flow_rate), which
describes transported mass per time rather than travel duration, and it
provides the thermal-delay correction relevant to [total thermal coolant
absorbed power at wall](name:total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall).

items.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of fast ions of one species and charge state arising from random
motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field, averaged over the two
transverse directions.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast ions of one specified species and charge state is the
field-perpendicular principal component of their gyrotropic kinetic pressure
tensor. It describes stress from velocity fluctuations about that
population's mean flow, averaged over the two transverse directions.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse second central
moment of the fast-ion distribution:

$$
p_{\perp,s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{2}\int w_\perp^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_{\perp,s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion pressure
for species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_s$ is the
ion mass, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is that population's velocity
distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The quantity $w_\perp$ is the magnitude of
the component of $\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ perpendicular to the local
magnetic field, where $\mathbf{u}_{s,c}$ is the mean velocity of the
specified fast-ion population.

This quantity includes only the suprathermal ions of the specified species
and charge state, without summation over species or charge states. It
excludes thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure, and mean-flow momentum
flux. It is one transverse principal pressure, not the sum of the two
transverse stresses or the isotropic trace pressure.

Together with the field-parallel component, it specifies the gyrotropic
[fast-ion charge-state pressure](name:fast_ion_charge_state_pressure).
Summing over all charge states of the same ion species gives the
[perpendicular fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure);
summing additionally over all fast-ion species gives the [perpendicular
total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

items.name: oxygen_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Local number density of oxygen ions at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over
all positively charged ionization states.
items.documentation:
The oxygen ion number density is the local population density of oxygen ions
at the H-mode pedestal top, the core-side shoulder of the edge transport
barrier. The location is identified by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate at the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

The defining charge-state aggregation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{O}} = \sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the total oxygen ion number density, $q$ is the
positive integer charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$ is the number
density of oxygen ions in charge state $q$.

This quantity is specific to oxygen and is evaluated locally at the pedestal
top. It includes all positively charged oxygen states, from singly charged
through fully stripped oxygen, and excludes neutral oxygen and ions of other
species. It is distinct from the [oxygen ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:oxygen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which applies the same
charge-state aggregation at the plasma boundary rather than at the pedestal
top.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport
items.description:
Parallel current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
conventional-charge flux along the local magnetic field attributed to
turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.
items.documentation:
Parallel current density due to anomalous transport is the signed
field-aligned projection of the conventional electric-current contribution
attributed to turbulent, nonclassical plasma transport.

The defining projection is

$$
j_\parallel = \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}} \cdot \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $j_\parallel$ is the parallel anomalous current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{anom}}$ is the [anomalous-transport current-density
vector](name:current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The
projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.

This quantity is a local component of the net anomalous current
contribution, with no individual species selected and no spatial averaging
implied. It excludes current contributions attributed to other mechanisms
and is not the total parallel plasma current density.

Unlike the [toroidal anomalous current
density](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport), which
projects onto the geometric toroidal direction, this component follows the
local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the anomalous contribution to conventional
electric current flows along the local magnetic-field vector.

items.name: ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency
items.description:
Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state, characterizing its
bulk rotational motion; each resolved component is determined from the
corresponding bulk-flow component and its geometric rotation lever arm.
items.documentation:
Angular velocity vector of a specified ion charge state is the vector of
angular rates associated with the bulk flow of that charge-state population.
It is charge-state-resolved and excludes density-weighted averaging over
other charge states.

For any resolved angular coordinate $q$, the component is the corresponding
bulk-flow velocity component divided by the geometric rotation lever arm for
that coordinate:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{A}} \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta}\,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}, \qquad \Omega^{q}_{i,\zeta} = \frac{\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}}{h_q}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{i,\zeta}$ is the ion-charge-state
rotation-frequency vector, $i$ labels the ion species, $\zeta$ labels the
charge state, $\mathcal{A}$ is the set of resolved angular coordinate
directions, $\mathbf{v}_{i,\zeta}$ is the bulk velocity vector of the same
charge-state population, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{q}$ is the positive tangent
direction of angular coordinate $q$, and $h_q=|\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial
q|$ is its geometric rotation lever arm. For the toroidal component in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, $q=\phi$ and
$h_\phi=R$, so the component is the [toroidal ion-charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency).

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved counterpart of [ion rotation
frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency). The charge-state-aggregated ion
quantity is the density-weighted mean over charge states, not a sum, because
rotation frequency is an intensive bulk-flow quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component corresponds to motion in
the positive tangent direction of its associated angular coordinate; in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the toroidal component is
positive for motion in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: oxygen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Instantaneous oxygen injection rate from gas fueling, expressed on an
equivalent-electron basis with eight equivalent electrons assigned to each
oxygen atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of oxygen atoms supplied by
gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron weighting. It
describes injected oxygen input, not the subsequent oxygen population or its
ionization state.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined from the oxygen-atom
injection rate by:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}(t) = 8\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t)
$$

where $t$ is physical time, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq,O}}(t)$ is the oxygen
source rate on the equivalent-electron basis, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t)$ is
the injected oxygen-atom rate, and the factor $8$ is the atomic number of
oxygen.

The scope is oxygen introduced by gas injection; contributions from other
species and from non-gas-injection sources are excluded. The rate is
instantaneous and aggregates the injected oxygen amount over the
gas-injection input, weighting each oxygen atom by eight equivalent
electrons. This bookkeeping weighting does not represent physical
free-electron production and does not resolve oxygen charge states.

Time integration of this rate over the post-breakdown interval gives the
corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory represented by
[accumulated oxygen count due to gas
injection](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection); unlike that
quantity, this standard name denotes the instantaneous source rate.

items.name: resistance_of_passive_loop
items.description:
Ohmic resistance of one passive conducting loop, relating its induced
current to the resistive voltage drop and determining dissipation during
electromagnetic transients.
items.documentation:
The electrical resistance of a passive conducting loop is the
proportionality between its current and the voltage drop caused by ohmic
dissipation. It represents irreversible conversion of electrical energy into
heat in the conducting path.

$$
V_R = R_{\rm loop} I_{\rm loop}
$$

where $V_R$ is the resistive voltage drop in volts, $I_{\rm loop}$ is the
loop current in amperes, and $R_{\rm loop}$ is the resistance in ohms. For a
uniform conductor, the resistance is governed by $R_{\rm loop}=\rho\ell/A$,
where $\rho$ is electrical resistivity, $\ell$ is conductor length, and $A$
is cross-sectional area. The current is the [current of a passive
loop](name:current_of_passive_loop). This quantity excludes inductive
voltage and describes only the ohmic contribution; together with the loop
self-inductance, it determines the resistive electromagnetic decay
timescale. It is the loop-level counterpart of the [resistance of a vacuum
vessel](name:resistance_of_vacuum_vessel) and depends on the conductor
material described by its [resistivity](name:resistivity_of_wall_material).

items.name: elongation_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Elongation of a flux surface is the ratio of its poloidal cross-section’s
vertical extent to its radial extent, independent of overall size.
items.documentation:
Elongation of flux surface

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining
relation is:

$$
\kappa = (Z_{\max} - Z_{\min})/(R_{\max} - R_{\min})
$$

where $\kappa$ is the elongation, $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the maximum
and minimum vertical coordinates of the cross-section, and $R_{\max}$ and
$R_{\min}$ are its maximum and minimum major radii.

The quantity applies to an individual flux surface, not an average over
nested surfaces. For an elliptical cross-section, it equals the ratio of the
vertical to horizontal semi-axes; the extent-based definition does not
require an ellipse. It is not restricted to the plasma boundary: evaluating
it there gives the [elongation of the plasma
boundary](name:elongation_of_plasma_boundary).

The [derivative of elongation with respect to normalized minor
radius](name:derivative_of_elongation_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_normalized_minor_radius)
describes how this ratio changes between neighboring surfaces, rather than
the shape ratio itself.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a
nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$,
$\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Absorbed coherent-wave power transferred directly to thermal ions of one
species inside a magnetic flux surface, summed over charge states and
resolved by toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
Thermal ion absorbed wave power per toroidal mode is the cumulative rate of
direct energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to the bulk,
approximately Maxwellian ions of one selected species inside a closed
magnetic flux surface. Each contribution corresponds to one toroidal Fourier
harmonic.

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}(\mathcal S) = \int_{V(\mathcal S)} q_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}\,dV
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the cumulative absorbed power, $i$
identifies the selected ion species, $\mathrm{th}$ denotes its thermal
population, $n_\phi$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, $\mathcal
S$ is the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\mathcal S)$ is its enclosed
plasma volume, $q_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{(n_\phi)}$ is the local absorbed wave
power density summed over all charge states of that species for the same
harmonic, and $dV$ is a volume element.

The quantity is summed over all charge states of the selected species, but
not over ion species or toroidal modes. It is an enclosed-volume integral,
not a local power density or necessarily a whole-plasma total. It excludes
direct absorption by fast ions and electrons, energy remaining in the wave
field, and energy subsequently redistributed between particle populations by
collisions.

Its charge-state-resolved contributions are represented by
[per-toroidal-mode thermal ion charge-state
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power); summing those
contributions over all charge states recovers this quantity. Summing over
all toroidal-mode contributions at a flux surface enclosing the entire
plasma recovers [thermal ion absorbed wave
power](name:thermal_ion_absorbed_wave_power) for the same ion species and
coherent-wave field.

items.name: helium_3_density
items.description:
Local number density of charged helium-3 ions, obtained by summing their
populations over all included ionization states at a plasma location.
items.documentation:
Helium-3 ion number density is the local count of charged helium-3 ions per
unit plasma volume at a specified plasma location. It is summed over the
singly ionized and fully stripped charge states and excludes neutral
helium-3 atoms.

$$
n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{Z=1}^{2} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},Z}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the plasma location, $Z$ is the ionic charge state,
and $n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He},Z}$ is the number density of helium-3 ions in
charge state $Z$, expressed in m$^{-3}$. The [volume-averaged helium-3
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density) and [line-averaged helium-3
density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) are spatial averages of this
local quantity over their respective domains.

items.name: plasma_electrical_conductivity
items.description:
Local plasma electrical-conductivity tensor mapping the electric-field
vector to the conductive current-density vector, including anisotropic
diagonal and off-diagonal coupling.
items.documentation:
Plasma electrical conductivity is the local rank-two material response that
relates the plasma electric field to the conductive electric-current
density. It represents the collective plasma response without selecting a
particular species, orbit class, direction, or transport mechanism.

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}} = \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}} \cdot \mathbf{E}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive
electric-current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is
the plasma electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\mathbf{E}$ is the
electric-field vector. In components, $J_i = \sigma_{ij}E_j$, where $i$
identifies the current-density direction and $j$ identifies the
electric-field direction. The tensor may be represented in the right-handed
cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, or in the
magnetic-field-aligned basis $(\hat{b},\hat{e}_{\perp 1},\hat{e}_{\perp
2})$, where $\hat{b}$ is the local magnetic-field direction.

The full tensor retains all diagonal and off-diagonal couplings and is
therefore broader than any single component coefficient. It excludes
displacement current and contributions that are not the local conductive
response of the plasma. The [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity),
[toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity), and [vertical
conductivity](name:vertical_conductivity) are diagonal component instances
in the cylindrical frame; [poloidal
conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity) and [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) are corresponding projections in
flux-surface-tangent and magnetic-field-aligned directions, respectively.

items.name: major_length_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Geometric length of the alpha-inclined major side of a parallelogram-shaped
cross-section belonging to a passive conductor element.
items.documentation:
The alpha-inclined side length is the geometric length of a
parallelogram-shaped cross-section of a passive conductor element.

For the two endpoints of the alpha side, the length is defined by

$$
\ell_{\alpha} = \left\|\mathbf{r}_{\alpha,2} - \mathbf{r}_{\alpha,1}\right\|
$$

where $\ell_{\alpha}$ is the alpha-side length, $\mathbf{r}_{\alpha,1}$ and
$\mathbf{r}_{\alpha,2}$ are the position vectors of its endpoints, and
$\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm. The side is inclined at angle $\alpha$ to
the outward major-radius direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to one passive conductor element and selects its
alpha-inclined, major side; it is not an electrical or material property and
is not aggregated over sides or elements. The parent [length of passive loop
element](name:length_of_passive_loop_element) denotes the corresponding
inclined-side length without selecting one side, while [minor length of
passive loop element](name:minor_length_of_passive_loop_element) describes
the complementary beta-inclined side.

items.name: parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description:
Dimensionless parallel flux-limiter coefficient that scales the
free-streaming bound on the parallel momentum-flux-density magnitude,
projected along the local magnetic-field unit vector, for a specified
neutral particle state in edge-plasma transport closures.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral-state momentum coefficient is a dimensionless
flux-limiter factor assigned to a specified neutral particle state in
edge-plasma transport closures. It scales the free-streaming bound on the
magnitude of the parallel component of neutral momentum-flux density, with
the projection taken along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

The cap set by the parallel coefficient is:

$$
\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm lim} = c_{\parallel}\,\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm FS}
$$

where $\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm lim}$ is the nonnegative limiter bound on the
magnitude of the modeled parallel neutral-state momentum-flux density,
$\Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm FS}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming bound for the
same field-aligned projection, and $c_{\parallel}$ is this coefficient. The
signed projected flux satisfies $|\Pi_{\parallel}| \le \Pi_{\parallel}^{\rm
lim}$; when flux limiting is active, $c_{\parallel}$ is bounded in $[0, 1]$.

This quantity is the parallel projection component of the vector
[neutral-state momentum flux-limiter
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region);
relative to that vector quantity, the specialization is the field-aligned
projection, not a different species or state aggregation. The coefficient
itself is a nonnegative cap and carries no directional sign, so it limits
the magnitude of the parallel momentum-flux-density component without
reversing the signed component. It differs from the
[radial](name:radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
[toroidal](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient),
and
[vertical](name:vertical_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
coefficients, which use $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ projections
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and from the
[poloidal](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient)
coefficient, which uses the poloidal projection.

items.name: xenon_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Number density of the xenon species at the divertor target is the local
particle count per volume for xenon ions at the sheath entrance immediately
upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the xenon-specific
member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local xenon ion number density is defined by the differential particle
count:

$$
n_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$
is the number of included xenon ions, and $V$ is a local plasma volume whose
center approaches the sheath entrance from the plasma side.

This quantity applies to the xenon-ion population immediately adjacent to
one divertor target and is summed over all positive xenon ionization states,
from singly ionized through fully stripped xenon. Neutral xenon atoms are
excluded; this is a local sheath-entrance density, not a volume-averaged
density or a density at a general plasma location.

Compared with [xenon_density](name:xenon_density), which denotes xenon ion
density at a general plasma point, this quantity is specialized to the
divertor-target sheath entrance. Its charge-state-summed species convention
parallels
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target),
with xenon replacing oxygen.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number
items.description:
Mean ionization state of a specified charge-state bundle of one ion species,
weighted locally by charge-state concentration and then averaged over the
plasma volume.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the plasma-volume average of the local
concentration-weighted mean ionic charge number within a specified
charge-state bundle of one ion species. Charge-state averaging within the
bundle precedes spatial volume averaging.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V \overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}\,dV
$$

where $V$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and
$\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the local [bundle-averaged ionic charge
number](name:ion_charge_state_average_charge_number). Locally,
$\overline{Z}_{\mathcal{B}} = \sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}} q x_q$, where
$\mathcal{B}$ is the specified bundle, $q$ is the ionic charge number, and
$x_q$ is the local number-density fraction of charge state $q$ within that
bundle, with $\sum_{q\in\mathcal{B}}x_q = 1$.

Only charge states within the specified bundle contribute; different ion
species are not combined. The spatial average uses volume weighting without
additional ion-density weighting, so it is not generally equal to the ratio
of total ionic charge to total ion number over the plasma. For a bundle
containing one fixed charge state, the result equals that state's charge
number.

This first charge-number moment is distinct from the [bundle mean-square
charge number](name:square_of_ion_charge_state_charge_number), which
averages the squared ionic charge number rather than the charge number.

items.name: total_incident_power_at_wall
items.description:
Total plasma power arriving at all plasma-facing wall surfaces, summed over
conducted, convected, radiative, and other incident energy channels.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total energy delivered from the plasma to plasma-facing
wall and divertor surfaces by all incident channels. It represents the
area-integrated power arriving at those surfaces before reflection or
re-emission.

The total incident power is defined by integrating the incident energy-flux
density over the complete plasma-facing area:

$$
P_{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf r)\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the total incident power, $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is
the union of the relevant plasma-facing surfaces, $q_{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf
r)$ is the incident power per unit area at surface position $\mathbf r$, and
$\mathrm{d}A$ is a differential surface area. The integrand is the
area-density counterpart energy flux at wall. The total includes all
incident energy channels and excludes power emitted from the wall toward the
plasma or vacuum.

items.name: parallel_fast_particle_energy
items.description:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the volume-integrated energy content of the
parallel degree of freedom of a specified suprathermal particle population,
defined as three-halves of its parallel-pressure integral.
items.documentation:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the energy content associated with the
parallel degree of freedom of a specified suprathermal particle population.
It is integrated over the plasma volume, rather than being a local energy
density.

The defining pressure-integral relation is:

$$
W_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{\mathcal{V}} p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}\,dV
$$

where $W_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-particle energy,
$\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume, $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the
parallel pressure of the specified fast-particle population, and $dV$ is a
differential volume element.

The integral covers the plasma volume and the specified fast (suprathermal)
population. It excludes bulk thermal particles and the population's
perpendicular-motion contribution; contributions over the volume are
accumulated, not averaged.

This is the parallel contribution to [fast-particle
energy](name:fast_particle_energy). The [perpendicular fast-particle
energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) is the corresponding
contribution from motion perpendicular to the local magnetic field;
together, these directional contributions distinguish the components of the
same population's kinetic energy.

items.name: accumulated_lithium_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of lithium introduced by gas
injection during plasma prefill, assigning three count units to each lithium
atom.
items.documentation:
The accumulated lithium prefill count is the equivalent-electron inventory
of lithium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown. Each lithium
atom contributes three equivalent-electron counts, corresponding to its
atomic number.

The defining accumulation is

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}} = Z_{\mathrm{Li}} N_{\mathrm{Li}} = 3\int_{t_{\mathrm{start}}}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq,Li}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory,
$Z_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is lithium's atomic number, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the
introduced lithium-atom inventory, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium
injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{start}}$ is the prefill start time, and
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity describes delivered lithium inventory during prefill, not the
instantaneous [lithium source
rate](name:lithium_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), post-breakdown
[accumulated lithium
count](name:accumulated_lithium_count_due_to_gas_injection), or the
inventory of all injected species represented by [accumulated total prefill
gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count).

items.name: line_averaged_nitrogen_density
items.description:
Line-averaged number density of all nitrogen nuclei along a specified plasma
chord, summed over every ionization state from neutral through fully
stripped nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Line-averaged nitrogen density is the chord-length average of the local
number density of all nitrogen nuclei, including every nitrogen ionization
state from neutral nitrogen through fully stripped nitrogen.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_N = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_N(\ell)\,d\ell
$$

where $n_N(\ell)$ is the local charge-state-summed nitrogen density defined
by [nitrogen density](name:nitrogen_density), $\ell$ is distance along the
specified chord, and $L$ is the total chord length.

This quantity is the chord-integrated nitrogen inventory divided by chord
length, so it preserves the density dimension while removing variation along
the chord. It is distinct from the spatially averaged [volume-averaged
nitrogen density](name:volume_averaged_nitrogen_density), which averages
over the plasma volume rather than a chord.

items.name: neon_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Neon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over
all ionization states.
items.documentation:
Neon ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local
concentration of ionized neon particles there, aggregated over their
ionization states.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{z=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the total neon ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{z+}}$ is the number density of neon ions with charge state
$z+$, $z$ is the positive integer charge state, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the
atomic number of neon and the maximum ion charge state.

This quantity applies to ionized neon at the top of the H-mode edge
pedestal, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux
coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is local
and summed over all neon ion charge states; it excludes neutral neon,
individual charge-state densities, and line-, surface-, or volume-averaged
densities.

It is the neon-species component of the aggregate [density at the pedestal
top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). In contrast, [neon density at the plasma
boundary](name:neon_density_at_plasma_boundary) describes the same
charge-state-summed neon population at a different spatial locus.

items.name: radial_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid
items.description:
Radial magnetic-field component at the geometric centroid of a ferritic
element, projected onto the outward major-radius direction in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the magnetic-field component evaluated at a ferritic
element’s geometric centroid and projected along the cylindrical
major-radius direction. It describes the applied magnetic field, not the
ferritic element’s magnetization.

The radial component is defined by

$$
B_R = \mathbf{B} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector and $\hat{R}$ is the outward
major-radius unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. The evaluation point is the ferritic-element centroid; its radial
location is given by the [radial coordinate of the ferritic element
centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid). Together
with the [vertical magnetic field at the ferritic element
centroid](name:vertical_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid) and
[toroidal magnetic field at the ferritic element
centroid](name:toroidal_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid), it
specifies the local field vector.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_R$ points toward increasing major radius
$R$.

items.name: thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by the bulk thermal ion population within the
plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The thermal-ion power at inside flux surface is the running volume integral
of wave power deposited into the bulk thermal ion population, giving the
radial distribution of enclosed thermal-ion wave absorption. It is the
bulk-ion component of
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
separated from both fast-ion and electron heating channels.

The quantity is the volume integral of the thermal-ion wave-power density
$p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r})$ over the plasma domain $V(\chi)$ enclosed by
the flux surface labeled $\chi$:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},i}(\chi) = \int_{V(\chi)} p_{\mathrm{th},i}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is the thermal-ion volumetric wave-power density
in W m$^{-3}$, $dV$ is the volume element in m$^3$, $P_{\mathrm{th},i}$ is
the enclosed thermal-ion wave power in W, and $\chi$ is the chosen
flux-surface label, such as the normalized toroidal flux radius
$\rho_\mathrm{tor,norm}$.

This quantity includes only wave energy absorbed by bulk thermal ions inside
the selected closed magnetic flux surface. Wave energy absorbed by thermal
electrons is
[thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
wave energy absorbed by suprathermal ions is
[fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface),
and the sum over thermal and fast ion populations is
[ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: lithium_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the lithium ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local lithium-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all lithium ionic charge states. It represents ionized
lithium specifically, rather than electrons, neutral lithium, or another
plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\sum_{q\ge 1} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li,axis}}$ is the total lithium-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the number of lithium ions, $V$ is
physical volume, $q$ is the positive integer labeling a lithium ionic charge
state, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of lithium ions in
charge state $q$.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete ionized lithium population at that
location and uses a sum over all lithium ionic charge states, not a density
for one selected charge state or a sum over different chemical elements. It
is neither a flux-surface nor volume integral and excludes neutral lithium.

This is the lithium-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the
same local-density and magnetic-axis scope as [deuterium density at the
magnetic axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts lithium
ions rather than deuterium ions; unlike [electron density at the magnetic
axis](name:electron_density_at_magnetic_axis), it does not count electrons.

items.name: deuterium_tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Deuterium-tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
is the local concentration of the effective single fuel pseudo-species at
the transport-barrier shoulder.
items.documentation:
Deuterium-tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
is the local concentration of the effective single deuterium-tritium fuel
pseudo-species at the inner shoulder of the H-mode transport barrier.

The local density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{DT}} = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{N_{\mathrm{DT}}(\Delta V)}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{DT}}$ is the deuterium-tritium pseudo-species number
density, $N_{\mathrm{DT}}(\Delta V)$ is the number of pseudo-species ions
within the volume $\Delta V$, and $\Delta V$ is a shrinking spatial volume
around the evaluation point.

This quantity applies to the effective single deuterium-tritium fuel
pseudo-species, rather than to separately resolved deuterium and tritium
populations. It is a local value at the pedestal top, whose position is
defined by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), and is not a
flux-surface or line-of-sight average.

It is the deuterium-tritium species specialization of [density at the
pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [deuterium-tritium
density at the plasma
boundary](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_plasma_boundary), which uses the
plasma boundary as its locus, this quantity is evaluated at the pedestal-top
location.

items.name: upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description:
The upper-inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce
(2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how the upper, high-field-side
quadrant of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface departs from a reference
ellipse; positive values are boxier and negative values are more
diamond-like or indented.
items.documentation:
The upper-inner squareness of a flux surface is the dimensionless Luce
(2013) shape coefficient that characterizes how the upper, high-field-side
quadrant of a nested toroidal magnetic flux surface departs from a reference
ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and
[elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface). It is the upper
quadrant-resolved component of
[inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface),
complementing
[lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface).
The upper-inner quadrant is the segment from the top of the surface to the
inner midplane, on the high-field side at smaller major radius in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and
$Z$ is vertical height.

The coefficient $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}$ enters the Luce parametric flux-surface
shape model as an additional harmonic beyond elongation $\kappa$ and
[triangularity](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface):

$$
Z(\theta)-Z_c = a\kappa\sin\!\left[\theta + \zeta_\mathrm{ui}\sin(2\theta)\right], \qquad \pi/2 \le \theta \le \pi
$$

where $Z(\theta)$ is the vertical coordinate of the contour, $Z_c$ is the
vertical coordinate of the surface center, $a$ is the horizontal half-width,
$\theta$ is the geometric poloidal angle measured about the surface center
in the $(R,Z)$ cross-section with $\theta=0$ at the outboard midplane and
increasing toward $+Z$, and $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}$ is the upper-inner
squareness coefficient. Setting $\zeta_\mathrm{ui}=0$ recovers the
corresponding reference ellipse for this quadrant.

This quantity is a quadrant-local squareness coefficient, not an average
over the two inner quadrants and not an outboard squareness coefficient in
the broader [squareness_of_flux_surface](name:squareness_of_flux_surface)
family. It describes corner shaping not represented by elongation or
triangularity alone.

Sign convention: Positive when the upper high-field-side corner of the
flux-surface cross-section is boxier than the reference ellipse; negative
values indicate a more diamond-like or indented corner.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Full physical extent of a rectangular Bragg crystal measured along its first
local tangential axis, the crystal-local X1 direction.
items.documentation:
The first-local-tangential width is the full physical extent of the
diffracting Bragg crystal along its crystal-local X1 axis.

For a rectangular crystal, the width is defined by the endpoint separation:

$$
w_{X_1}=x_{1,\max}-x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w_{X_1}$ is the first-local-tangential width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and
$x_{1,\min}$ are the maximum and minimum crystal-boundary coordinates along
the first local tangential axis.

This quantity applies only to rectangular crystal geometry and represents
the complete endpoint-to-endpoint extent of the diffracting crystal. It is
not a half-width, local chord, averaged dimension, spectral width, or
aperture width; no summation over multiple crystals is implied.

The companion transverse direction is identified by the [second local
tangential coordinate of the Bragg
crystal](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal), whereas
the [radius of the Bragg crystal](name:radius_of_bragg_crystal) describes a
center-to-edge distance for a circular active surface rather than a full
extent along X1.

items.name: hydrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the hydrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local hydrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the hydrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local hydrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all hydrogen ionic charge states. It represents
hydrogen ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral hydrogen, or
another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{H}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the hydrogen-ion number density at
the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ is the number of hydrogen ions summed
over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete hydrogen-ion population at that
location and is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor an electron or
neutral density.

This is the hydrogen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs
from [deuterium density at the magnetic
axis](name:deuterium_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts deuterium ions,
and from [hydrogenic density](name:hydrogenic_density), which aggregates
hydrogen-isotope populations rather than isolating hydrogen.

items.name: vertical_back_surface_curvature_of_optical_element
items.description:
Vertical back-surface curvature of an optical element is the signed
directional radius of curvature of the rear optical surface along the second
local tangential aperture direction. Here vertical means object-local
aperture vertical, not the Z direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical back-surface curvature of an optical element is the signed
directional radius of curvature of the back optical surface in its second
local tangential aperture direction. The right-handed local optical-surface
frame is $(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2, \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b)$ with
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1 \times \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 = \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$, where
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ are the first and second
surface-tangential aperture directions and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$ is the
positive normal of the back surface; this quantity uses
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$, the object-local aperture vertical direction.

The defining relation is the reciprocal of the signed normal curvature of
the back-surface normal section tangent to $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$:

$$
R_{b,2} = \frac{1}{\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)}
$$

where $R_{b,2}$ is the vertical back-surface curvature of the optical
element and $\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)$ is the signed normal
curvature of the back surface in the $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ direction.

This is a local directional radius, not the scalar parent optical-element
curvature and not the direction-agnostic back-surface curvature. It equals
the first-direction radius only for locally spherical or otherwise
direction-independent curvature, and it is not a principal, sagittal, or
meridional radius unless the surface definition aligns $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$
with that direction. Together with an orthogonal directional radius it may
characterize simple aligned toroidal curvature, but it does not fully
characterize a general aspherical surface.

items.name: momentum_flux
items.description:
Rate of transport of linear momentum per unit area across an oriented
surface in the plasma, combining convective, isotropic pressure, and viscous
stress contributions from any species or population.
items.documentation:
The momentum flux describes the rate at which linear momentum crosses a unit
area of an oriented surface in the plasma. It encompasses the convective
ram-pressure term, the isotropic thermal pressure, and viscous or turbulent
stress contributions, and appears as the divergence term in the plasma fluid
momentum-balance equation.

The momentum-flux tensor for a single plasma fluid is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi} = \rho \mathbf{v}\mathbf{v} + p\,\mathbf{I} + \boldsymbol{\pi}
$$

where $\rho$ is the mass density, $\mathbf{v}$ the bulk flow velocity, $p$
the scalar pressure, $\mathbf{I}$ the identity tensor, and
$\boldsymbol{\pi}$ the viscous stress tensor. The momentum current through a
surface with outward unit normal $\hat{n}$ is
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}\cdot\hat{n}$.

This name is the structural parent for species- and direction-resolved
forms. Species-specific instances include [ion momentum
flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), and [plasma momentum
flux](name:plasma_momentum_flux), each summed over the relevant population.
Directional projections such as parallel momentum flux isolate field-aligned
transport, while [poloidal momentum flux](name:poloidal_momentum_flux)
captures cross-field transport through toroidally symmetric surfaces. The
complementary volume source density entering the momentum balance is given
by volumetric plasma momentum source.

items.name: height_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Full vertical extent of an ICRH antenna strap conductor cross-section,
measured parallel to the Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ,
Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The antenna-strap height is the full vertical extent of the rectangular
conductor cross-section, measured parallel to the $Z$ direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is a geometric
cross-section dimension, not the antenna elevation or its distance from the
plasma.

$$
H = Z_{\max} - Z_{\min}
$$

where $H$ is the strap height and $Z_{\max}$ and $Z_{\min}$ are the vertical
coordinates of the upper and lower cross-section boundaries. The dimension
is non-negative and complements the toroidal width of the antenna strap and
[thickness of the antenna strap](name:thickness_of_antenna_strap), which
describe the other conductor extents. For an annular cross-section, the
radial boundaries are specified by the [inner radius of the antenna
strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap) and [outer radius of the antenna
strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap).

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector angular-momentum
transfer rate per plasma volume delivered to a specified thermal ion charge
state from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing particles.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of
angular-momentum transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a
specified charge state from Coulomb collisions with the counter-passing
population.

With $\mathrm{cp}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density
is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the
local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the collisional force
density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by counter-passing
particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over
ionization states. This is the counter-passing contribution to [thermal ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and differs from the corresponding [co-passing
quantity](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by the collision-partner orbit class.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{cp}}$ points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: argon_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of argon ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the
local argon-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all
argon ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of argon ions evaluated at the magnetic axis is the
local argon-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all
argon ionic charge states. It represents argon ions specifically, rather
than electrons, neutrals, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ar},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ar}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ar},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the argon-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the number of argon ions summed over all
ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the gradient of the poloidal
magnetic flux vanishes. It applies to the complete ionic argon population at
that location and is charge-state summed; neutral argon is excluded. It is
