neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density for another species.

This is the argon-specific realization of [density at the magnetic
axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), with the population fixed to argon
ions and the aggregation fixed to a sum over ionic charge states. The
corresponding species specialization for oxygen is [oxygen density at the
magnetic axis](name:oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis), which uses the same
magnetic-axis locus but a different ion population.

items.name: flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Flux at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the wall-area density
of a recombination-caused transfer rate at the wall. It fixes the wall locus
and recombination cause; a more specific quantity specifies what is
transported, such as energy, and how incident populations, charge states,
channels, and products are aggregated.
items.documentation:
Flux at a plasma-facing wall due to recombination is the wall-area density
of a transfer rate attributable to charged plasma particles recombining into
lower-charge or neutral states at a plasma-facing material surface. It is
the common at-wall recombination-flux concept: the wall locus and
recombination cause are fixed, while the transported quantity is specified
by a more specific member.

For a member transporting an extensive quantity $X$, the local wall-area
density is defined by

$$
F_X^{\mathrm{rec,wall}} = \frac{d\dot{X}^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}}{dA}
$$

where $F_X^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}$ is the at-wall flux density of the
transported quantity $X$ due to recombination, $\dot{X}^{\mathrm{rec,wall}}$
is the corresponding recombination-at-wall transfer rate, $A$ is
plasma-facing wall surface area, and the superscript $\mathrm{rec,wall}$
identifies the recombination contribution at the wall.

The quantity applies only to plasma-facing wall surfaces and to
recombination events occurring at or mediated by those surfaces. For the
unqualified at-wall recombination contribution, the scope is inclusive over
contributing incident plasma populations and charge states, recombination
channels, and product species or internal states unless a more specific
member explicitly narrows one of those categories.

It is not a flux through an arbitrary surface, not a volume recombination
rate, and not the total wall flux from all plasma-wall interaction
mechanisms. It excludes contributions from non-recombination processes such
as direct impact energy transfer, ionization, sputtering, radiation, or
reflection unless those processes are part of the recombination channel
being specified.

The [energy flux at wall due to
recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the member
obtained by taking $X$ to be energy; it inherits the same at-wall
recombination locus and cause while adding the energy-specific
interpretation and its stated aggregation over incident-ion species, charge
states, recombination channels, and emitted products. The parent relation
itself does not impose energy weighting on every possible member; it defines
the shared wall-area-density form for the recombination contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the recombination contribution transports the
specified quantity from the material wall toward the plasma-facing side.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Non-negative radius-like toroidal-flux label identifying the magnetic flux
surface at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the non-negative, radius-like toroidal-flux label of the
magnetic flux surface at the H-mode [pedestal
top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the core-side
shoulder of the edge transport barrier. It locates that surface on the
physical toroidal-flux scale rather than specifying a geometric distance.

The coordinate is defined from enclosed toroidal magnetic flux by:

$$
\rho_{\rm tor} = \sqrt{\frac{\Phi_{\rm tor}}{\pi B_0}}
$$

where $\rho_{\rm tor}$ is the toroidal flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\rm tor}$ is
the enclosed toroidal magnetic flux, $B_0$ is the positive reference vacuum
toroidal-field magnitude that sets the coordinate scale, and $\pi$ is the
circular constant.

The value applies to the single nested magnetic flux surface passing through
the pedestal top. It is a local flux-surface label, not a flux-surface or
volume average, and it has no particle-population or charge-state
aggregation.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of the parent [toroidal flux
coordinate](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate), obtained by evaluating that
coordinate on the pedestal-top surface. Unlike the [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate at the pedestal
top](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top), it retains
the radius-like physical scale of the toroidal flux coordinate.

items.name: ratio_of_toroidal_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Ratio of an ion species' local toroidal bulk velocity, density-weighted over
all ionic charge states, to the local total magnetic-field magnitude.
items.documentation:
Ratio of the local toroidal component of an ion species' bulk velocity to
the magnitude of the local total magnetic field. It expresses signed
toroidal ion motion scaled by the inverse field magnitude.

For ion species $i$, the defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{V}_{i\phi} = \frac{v_{i\phi}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathcal{V}_{i\phi}$ is this ratio, $v_{i\phi}$ is the [toroidal ion
velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local total
magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its
[magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude). The index $i$ identifies the ion
species.

For each ion species, $v_{i\phi}$ is the density-weighted mean over all its
ionic charge states, not a sum of charge-state velocities or an average
across species; neutral particles are excluded. The toroidal component is
along $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.
The numerator and denominator refer to the same local position, with no
spatial aggregation.

The denominator is the magnitude of the total magnetic field, not a signed
toroidal or poloidal component. Multiplying the ratio by this magnitude
recovers the toroidal ion velocity. The [parallel ion velocity
ratio](name:ratio_of_parallel_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude)
instead uses the component along the magnetic-field direction, while the
[radial ion velocity
ratio](name:ratio_of_radial_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude) uses
the major-radius component.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion bulk-velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Volume-averaged thermal pressure of electrons in the scrape-off layer, the
open-field-line region between the last closed flux surface and material
plasma-facing components.
items.documentation:
Electron pressure over the scrape-off layer is the volume-averaged thermal
pressure of electrons in the open-field-line region between the last closed
flux surface and the material plasma-facing components. It represents the
electron partial-pressure contribution to [pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:pressure_over_scrape_off_layer) over that volume.

The volume average is defined from the local electron thermal pressure over
the scrape-off-layer volume:

$$
\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} \int_{V_{\mathrm{SOL}}} n_e(\mathbf{x}) T_e(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $\langle p_e \rangle_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the volume-averaged electron
pressure over the scrape-off layer, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron
number density, $T_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local electron temperature
expressed as thermal energy per electron, $V_{\mathrm{SOL}}$ is the
scrape-off-layer volume, $dV$ is a volume element, and $\mathbf{x}$ is
position.

This quantity excludes ion partial pressures and the neutral-gas pressure
described by [neutral pressure over the scrape-off
layer](name:neutral_pressure_over_scrape_off_layer). It is a SOL volume
average, not the electron pressure at the plasma boundary, and it is related
to electron density over the scrape-off layer through the same averaging
domain but is a density-temperature moment rather than a number-density
average.

items.name: minimum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description:
Lower allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant for
poloidal-field coils, with its magnitude and sign defined by one row of the
force-combination matrix.
items.documentation:
Minimum force of a poloidal-field coil is the lower allowable value of a
signed electromagnetic force resultant acting on the poloidal-field coil
system. Each row of the force-combination matrix defines one resultant by
weighting the radial and vertical components of the [force of a
poloidal-field coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For combination row $k$, the resultant is defined by

$$
F_{\mathrm{comb},k}=w_{kR}F_R+w_{kZ}F_Z
$$

where $F_R$ and $F_Z$ are the radial and vertical electromagnetic-force
components, $w_{kR}$ and $w_{kZ}$ are the row weights, and $k$ identifies
the combination row. The minimum value satisfies $F_{\min,k}\leq
F_{\mathrm{comb},k}$ for the applicable row. Unlike the [maximum force of a
poloidal-field coil](name:maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), this
quantity specifies the lower structural bound rather than the upper bound.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertical force component is directed
upward along $+Z$ and the radial force component is directed outward along
increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: deuterium_density
items.description:
Deuterium density is the number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion
population. It is the local density of deuterons, excluding neutral atoms,
molecules, and line- or volume-averaged deuterium densities.
items.documentation:
Deuterium density is the number density of ionized deuterium in the fuel-ion
population. As a species-level density it is charge-state-summed over
ionized atomic charge states; for deuterium this reduces to the singly
ionized deuteron population.

The local deuterium density is defined by the charge-state sum

$$
n_D = \sum_{q>0} n_{\mathrm{D}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium density, $q$ is the positive atomic charge
state, and $n_{\mathrm{D}^{q+}}$ is the number density of deuterium ions in
charge state $q$.

Neutral deuterium atoms, molecular deuterium, and non-deuterium species are
excluded. This quantity is local; spatial aggregations such as
[line-averaged deuterium density](name:line_averaged_deuterium_density) and
[volume-averaged deuterium density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density)
are distinct quantities.

items.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of carbon impurity ions at the
last closed magnetic flux surface, resolved along increasing toroidal angle.
items.documentation:
The carbon impurity-ion toroidal velocity at the plasma boundary is the
local density-weighted mean of the bulk-flow velocities of all included
carbon ion charge states on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is not
a flux-surface average; that distinct quantity is the toroidal
flux-surface-averaged carbon velocity, while the magnetic-axis counterpart
is [toroidal carbon velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

The defining local component is

$$
V_{\phi,C}(R,Z)=\frac{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\,\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_{q\in Q} n_{C^{q+}}(R,Z)}
$$

where $Q$ is the set of included carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is
the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $\mathbf{V}_{C^{q+}}$ is
its bulk velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The component is resolved in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$; $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal
angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when the carbon-ion bulk flow has a component in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of electrons evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier, where reduced cross-field turbulent
transport can sustain steep electron-density gradients.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of electrons evaluated on the flux surface assigned
to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the electron
population at that flux-surface location. Electrons are counted directly as
mobile negative charge carriers; no ion charge-state aggregation is
involved.

The number density is defined by

$$
n_e = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_e}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density in m$^{-3}$, $\Delta N_e$ is the
dimensionless number of electrons in the volume element, and $\Delta V$ is
the volume element in m$^{3}$.

This is the electron-specific member of [density at the internal transport
barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier). It is distinct from
ion density at the internal transport barrier, which counts ions rather than
electrons; in a quasineutral plasma the electron density is related to ion
charge densities at the same flux surface by charge balance. The internal
transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced
cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients.

items.name: radial_outline_of_wall
items.documentation:
The radial outline coordinate is the major-radius position of each point on
the boundary contour designated as the wall. It locates the contour relative
to the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical coordinate.

For a contour point identified by parameter $s$, the coordinate is defined
by

$$
R(s)=\mathbf{r}(s)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{R}}(s)
$$

where $\mathbf{r}(s)$ is the position vector of the contour point measured
from the machine symmetry axis, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}(s)$ is the local outward
radial unit vector, and $s$ identifies the point along the outline.

The quantity applies point-by-point to the specified wall contour and
carries no contour averaging, integration, maximum, or other spatial
aggregation. The generic wall locus does not by itself distinguish a first
wall, vacuum-vessel wall, or limiter surface; that physical boundary
identity is determined by the applicable wall definition. It is a radial
coordinate, not a vertical coordinate, toroidal coordinate, surface-normal
coordinate, or wall-normal distance.

Its meaning is analogous to [radial outline of a limiter
tile](name:radial_outline_of_limiter_tile), but the evaluated boundary
differs; [radial outline of a coil conductor
element](name:radial_outline_of_coil_conductor_element) likewise applies the
same radial-coordinate concept to a conductor contour rather than a wall
contour.

items.name: fast_particle_density
items.description:
Local or flux-surface-averaged concentration of suprathermal particles of a
selected species, including trapped and passing orbits and excluding thermal
particles.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle number density is the concentration of the suprathermal,
nonthermal population of a selected species. It includes all orbit classes
and may denote either a local density or its magnetic-flux-surface average.

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the fast-particle
distribution:

$$
n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\int f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle number density, $s$ labels
the selected species, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its fast-particle velocity
distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle
velocity, $t$ is time, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The flux-surface-averaged form is the differential-volume-weighted average
of this local moment over a magnetic flux surface. Superposed fast
populations of the same species contribute additively; different species are
not implicitly combined. For an ion species specified without charge-state
resolution, the fast-particle density is summed over all charge states.

This quantity is the fast-population contribution to [particle
density](name:particle_density), which also includes thermal particles. The
thermal population is excluded here; the name does not prescribe a universal
energy threshold separating the populations.

Orbit restrictions define [co-passing fast-particle
density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), [counter-passing
fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density), and
[trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density). For a
complete, nonoverlapping orbit partition, these contributions sum to the
fast-particle density when evaluated with the same species selection and
averaging convention. Volume integration, followed by summation over the
included species, gives the [total fast-particle
count](name:total_fast_particle_count).

items.name: energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Outgoing energy flux per unit plasma-facing wall area produced when incident
plasma ions recombine at the surface, summed over incident-ion species,
incident-ion charge states, recombination channels, and emitted product
species and states.
items.documentation:
Energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which
recombination-associated energy is emitted from a plasma-facing surface per
unit area as a result of incident plasma ions recombining or neutralizing at
the material boundary. It is the total outgoing energy flux carried by
emitted recombination products or quanta, not the incident plasma energy
flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The total recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ is
defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing recombination source:

$$
Q_\mathrm{rec}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{i,\,\zeta,\,c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion
charge state, $c$ the surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$
the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission
class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space
by an emitted product or quantum, and
$d\Gamma_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing
recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For
discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding
sum.

This quantity is the energy-weighted counterpart of particle flux at the
wall due to recombination, which counts the same surface recombination
source without energy weighting, and is the energy-flux realization of [flux
at the wall due to recombination](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).
The incident-ion decomposition is charge-state-summed in this total: [ion
charge-state energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
resolves a specified incident-ion species and charge state, while [ion
energy flux at the wall due to
recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) is the
corresponding ion contribution after summing over charge states.
Neutral-product particle specializations such as [neutral particle flux at
the wall due to
recombination](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination)
partition emitted-product counts and do not by themselves include energy
weighting.

Sign convention: Positive when recombination-associated energy is emitted
away from the plasma-facing wall surface into the plasma-facing half-space.

items.name: neon_density_at_divertor_target
items.description:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance, summed over Ne1+ through Ne10+ and
excluding neutral neon.
items.documentation:
Number density of neon ions at the divertor target is the local particle
count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the
target-facing plasma boundary. It is the neon-specific member of
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target).

The local neon-ion number density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne}} = \sum_{q=1}^{10} \frac{dN_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the neon-ion number density,
$N_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+}}$ is the number of neon ions in charge state $q+$
within the local plasma volume $V$, $V$ is the local plasma volume, and $q$
is the positive integer neon charge-state number. The upper limit 10 denotes
fully stripped neon.

This quantity applies to the free neon-ion population immediately adjacent
to the divertor target on the plasma side of the electrostatic sheath. It is
summed over all positive neon charge states from Ne1+ through Ne10+,
counting each ion once; neutral neon atoms are excluded. It is not the
density of all ion species or the free-electron population represented by
[electron_density_at_divertor_target](name:electron_density_at_divertor_target).

This member specializes
[density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target) by selecting
neon ions while retaining the same target-sheath evaluation locus. It is the
species-specific counterpart of related quantities such as
[oxygen_density_at_divertor_target](name:oxygen_density_at_divertor_target).

items.name: neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Outgoing neutral-particle number flux density from recombination at a
plasma-facing wall, summed over emitted neutral species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Recombination-associated neutral particle flux at a plasma-facing wall is
the rate per unit wall area at which neutral products leave the surface and
enter the adjacent plasma. It counts particles rather than the energy or
momentum they carry.

The flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outgoing
recombination-associated neutral particle-number flux density,
$N_{\mathrm{rec}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the corresponding number of emitted
neutral particles, $A$ is plasma-facing wall area, and $t$ is time.

The quantity applies to neutral products generated when incident plasma ions
recombine or neutralize at the wall. It is summed over contributing
incident-ion species and charge states, recombination channels, emitted
neutral species, and emitted internal states. It excludes energy weighting
and therefore differs from
[energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

This neutral emitted-particle quantity is the neutral-product specialization
of particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination. It is distinct from
[incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which counts recombination-associated neutral particles arriving at the
wall, and from
[neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination),
which resolves the emitted flux by internal state.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral particles travel from the
plasma-facing wall into the adjacent plasma.

items.name: neutral_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Effective convection velocity for the pressure-gradient diamagnetic
contribution to neutral-species momentum transport, retaining transport
direction rather than only speed.
items.documentation:
The neutral diamagnetic momentum-convection velocity is the effective vector
coefficient assigned to the pressure-gradient-associated diamagnetic
contribution to neutral momentum transport. It is distinct from the total
mean velocity of neutral particles.

For a selected component of neutral momentum density, its constitutive role
is:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{\pi,\ast} = \pi^{0}\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}$ is the effective diamagnetic convection
velocity, $\pi^{0}$ is the selected component of neutral momentum density,
and $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^{0}_{\pi,\ast}$ is its associated convective
momentum-flux vector. The superscript $0$ denotes the neutral population,
and the subscript $\ast$ identifies the diamagnetic contribution.

The quantity applies to a selected neutral species without selecting an
individual internal state; no aggregation over different neutral species is
implied. An internal-state-resolved counterpart, [neutral-state velocity due
to diamagnetic drift](name:neutral_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift),
instead applies to one specified neutral state.

The diamagnetic attribution identifies an effective momentum-transport
contribution, not a Lorentz-force drift of electrically neutral particles.
Consequently, a charged-particle diamagnetic-drift formula does not define
this coefficient, and perpendicularity to the magnetic field is not implied.
Diffusive momentum transport and other convection contributions are
excluded.

This is the neutral momentum-transport member of the [velocity due to
diamagnetic drift](name:velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) family. Its
[neutral velocity magnitude due to diamagnetic drift] is the norm
$|\mathbf{v}^{0}_{\ast}|$, which discards the transport direction.

Sign convention: Positive when a velocity component advects positive neutral
momentum density along the specified positive direction of that component.

items.name: power_due_to_conduction
items.description:
Thermal power deposited on one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron
and ion conduction along scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines, excluding
convective, radiative, and neutral-particle power.
items.documentation:
Conductive deposited power is thermal power transferred from
scrape-off-layer plasma to one or more plasma-facing surfaces by electron
and ion heat conduction along magnetic field lines. The selected surface may
be an individual target, a divertor assembly, or a collection of wall and
divertor surfaces.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{cond}} = \int_S \left(\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the deposited power, $S$ is the selected
plasma-facing surface, $\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ and
$\mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ are the electron and ion
conductive heat-flux vectors, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed
from the plasma toward the material, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface-area
element.

The quantity excludes convective enthalpy, radiative absorption, and
neutral-particle bombardment. A single-target instance is represented by
[power at divertor target due to
conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction), while the
corresponding all-channel energy flux density is distinguished by [energy
flux at divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target).

items.name: energy_confinement_time
items.description:
Characteristic timescale for loss of confined plasma thermal energy, defined
as stored thermal energy divided by the net power leaving that energy
reservoir.
items.documentation:
Energy confinement time is the characteristic timescale on which the
confined plasma loses its stored thermal energy through net outward energy
transport and other thermal-energy loss channels. The stored energy is the
volume-integrated quantity defined by [thermal plasma
energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), not a particle confinement time or the
duration of plasma confinement.

$$
\tau_E = \frac{W_{\mathrm{th}}}{P_{\mathrm{loss}}}
$$

where $\tau_E$ is the energy confinement time, $W_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the
stored thermal energy in J, and $P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ is the net power loss
from that thermal-energy reservoir in W. In a stationary power balance,
$P_{\mathrm{loss}}$ equals the net heating power deposited in the plasma. It
is distinct from plasma confinement time, which denotes the elapsed duration
of confinement rather than an energy-loss timescale.

items.name: co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local Coulomb-collisional power transferred from co-passing fast particles
to fast ions of a specified species per unit volume, summed over all ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Co-passing fast-ion collisional power density is the local rate at which
Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from co-passing fast particles to
the fast-ion population of a specified ion species. The co-passing
designation identifies the donor particles' passing orbit class; it does not
restrict the receiving ions to that orbit class.

The power density is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision
operator acting on the receiving fast ions:

$$
P_{i\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{q\in Q_i} \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} \frac{1}{2}m_{iq}v^2 C_{iq\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}[f_{iq},f_{f,\mathrm{co}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i\leftarrow f,\mathrm{co}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this power density;
$i$ identifies the receiving fast-ion species; $Q_i$ is the set of its ionic
charge states; $q$ identifies a charge state; $m_{iq}$ is the mass of ions
in that state; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is receiving-ion
velocity and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed; $f_{iq}$ is the distribution of
receiving fast ions in charge state $q$; $f_{f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the
distribution of co-passing donor fast particles; $C_{iq\leftarrow
f,\mathrm{co}}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional
rate of change of the receiving distribution due to those donors; and $d^3v$
is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the receiving
ions' full velocity space.

The quantity is local and is summed over all charge states of the specified
receiving ion species, not averaged over charge states or summed over
different ion species. The co-passing restriction applies to the donor fast
particles; counter-passing and trapped donors are excluded. This is an
energy-transfer rate, not stored kinetic-energy density, and it excludes
energy deposited in thermal ions. The [co-passing fast-ion charge-state
collisional power
density](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions)
resolves a single receiving ionic charge state rather than summing over
charge states.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic
energy of the receiving fast-ion population.

items.name: difference_of_vacuum_poloidal_current_function_and_initial_vacuum_poloidal_current_function
items.description:
Signed change in the combined external-coil vacuum poloidal current function
relative to its initial reference value, representing variation of the
toroidal field multiplied by major radius.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed difference between the present and initial values
of the vacuum poloidal current function produced by external coil currents.
It represents the change in the major-radius-weighted toroidal magnetic
field in the axisymmetric current-free vacuum region.

Let $F_{\rm vac}$ denote the [vacuum poloidal current
function](name:vacuum_poloidal_current_function). Its change relative to the
initial reference state is

$$
\Delta F_{\rm vac}=F_{\rm vac}-F_{\rm vac,initial}=R B_{\phi,\rm vac}-R B_{\phi,\rm vac,initial}
$$

where $\Delta F_{\rm vac}$ is the signed change, $F_{\rm vac}$ is the
present external-coil vacuum poloidal current function, $F_{\rm
vac,initial}$ is its value in the initial reference state, $R$ is major
radius, and $B_{\phi,\rm vac}$ is the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field
component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $\phi$ is
toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity uses the combined vacuum contribution from external coil
currents and excludes plasma currents and induced currents in conducting
structures. It is a difference from one initial reference value, not the
absolute [vacuum poloidal current
function](name:vacuum_poloidal_current_function); within an axisymmetric
current-free region, it inherits the parent function's spatial constancy.

Sign convention: Positive when the present value of $R B_{\phi,\rm vac}$
exceeds its initial reference value, with $B_{\phi,\rm vac}$ positive in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field
items.description:
The perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the complex first-order vector
eigenfunction of the magnetic-field perturbation for a single toroidal
harmonic in the current-free vacuum region surrounding the plasma. It is
defined relative to the background vacuum magnetic field and excludes the
equilibrium field while retaining all spatial components.
items.documentation:
The perturbed vacuum magnetic field $\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}$
is the complex first-order vector eigenfunction of the magnetic-field
perturbation for a single toroidal harmonic in the current-free exterior
domain surrounding the plasma. It is defined relative to the background
[vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field), retains all spatial
components, and excludes the equilibrium field itself.

For this single-toroidal-mode quantity, the real time-dependent perturbation
is reconstructed from the complex amplitude by

$$
\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}(R,\phi,Z,t) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}(R,Z)\exp\!\left(i n\phi - i\omega t\right)\right]
$$

where $\delta\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the real magnetic-field
perturbation, $\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the complex
eigenfunction defined here, $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical
frame with $R$ major radius, $\phi$ the toroidal angle increasing
counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ vertical
height, $t$ is time, $\operatorname{Re}$ takes the real part, $i$ is the
imaginary unit, $n$ is the [toroidal MHD mode
number](name:toroidal_mhd_mode_number), and $\omega$ is the angular
eigenfrequency. The chosen temporal factor fixes the phase convention; using
the opposite temporal factor complex-conjugates the eigenfunction, and the
overall complex scale and phase are set only by an explicit normalization.

In the current-free vacuum domain, absence of free current and magnetic
monopoles requires
$\nabla\times\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}=\mathbf{0}$ and
$\nabla\cdot\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}=0$, where $\nabla$ is the
spatial derivative operator and $\mathbf{0}$ is the zero vector.
Equivalently, $\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}=-\nabla\delta\Phi$ with
$\nabla^2\delta\Phi=0$, where $\delta\Phi$ is the scalar magnetic potential
of the perturbation; this potential is defined up to an additive constant.
At the plasma-vacuum interface, the normal component of this vacuum
perturbation is the exterior counterpart of the plasma-side perturbed
magnetic field used for interface matching.

The scope is the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma and inside
the relevant conducting or far-field boundary; it does not include
current-carrying plasma regions or free-current regions in material
structures. The quantity is one complex vector for one toroidal mode number,
with no averaging over phase, space, or mode number and no summation over
multiple toroidal harmonics. It is distinct from scalar field strength, from
the unperturbed [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field), and
from any real physical perturbation before the normal-mode reconstruction is
applied.

The vector decomposes in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame as
projections on $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$; the
[radial](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) and
[toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) quantities are
component projections of the same complex eigenfunction. The [poloidal
projection](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) is defined
relative to the explicitly chosen flux-coordinate system $(s,\theta,\phi)$
for that component and is not the cylindrical $Z$ projection. The
decomposition
$\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_\mathrm{vac}=\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{vac},\mathrm{Re}}+i\tilde{\delta\mathbf{B}}_{\mathrm{vac},\mathrm{Im}}$
separates real and imaginary phase quadratures; component quantities such as
the [radial real
part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part), [radial
imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part),
and [poloidal real
part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) are
projections or quadratures of this parent vector.

Sign convention: Positive when a real component projection of the
reconstructed perturbation points along its positive basis direction, with
$+\hat{R}$ increasing major radius, $+\hat{\phi}$ increasing toroidal angle
$\phi$, and $+\hat{Z}$ increasing vertical height in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_mode_number
items.description:
Dimensionless non-negative integer labeling the radial branch of a linear
MHD eigenmode by its number of radial nodes between the magnetic axis and
plasma boundary.
items.documentation:
Radial mode number is a dimensionless integer branch index that specifies
the radial branch of a linear MHD perturbation. It identifies radial
structure rather than periodicity in either angular direction.

The radial branch index is defined by

$$
n_r = N_{\mathrm{nodes}}[\xi(\rho)]
$$

where $n_r$ is the radial mode number, $\xi(\rho)$ is the radial
eigenfunction, $N_{\mathrm{nodes}}$ counts its interior zeros, and $\rho$ is
the radial coordinate within the flux-coordinate set $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$;
the count is taken between the magnetic axis and the plasma boundary.

The radial mode number is one component of the mode number, distinct from
the angular harmonics represented by the [poloidal mode
number](name:poloidal_mode_number) and [toroidal MHD mode
number](name:toroidal_mhd_mode_number).

items.name: decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Characteristic outward distance over which a decaying plasma quantity
decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for a plasma quantity that decreases
outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer.
The operand may be a particle density, temperature, or heat-flux magnitude.

$$
L_f = \left|\frac{d\ln f}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_f$ is the e-folding length, $f$ is the positive scalar quantity or
magnitude being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined
plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is
defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero.

The general quantity includes the electron number-density specialization
[electron decay length](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer),
the ion number-density specialization ion decay length, and the heat-flux
specialization [heat decay
length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It does not select a
species, transport channel, or particular decaying quantity.

items.name: toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient
items.description:
Toroidal flux coordinate gradient is the spatial variation of a flux-surface
label based on enclosed toroidal magnetic flux. It denotes the gradient
family itself, without fixing a particular norm, projection, component, or
flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Toroidal flux coordinate gradient is the spatial gradient of a flux-surface
label $\chi$ constructed from toroidal magnetic flux. It represents the
underlying gradient concept from which scalar measures, components,
projections, and averages of the coordinate variation are defined.

The relation between the coordinate change and the gradient is:

$$
d\chi = \nabla \chi \cdot d\mathbf{x}
$$

where $\chi$ is the toroidal-flux-based flux coordinate, $\nabla \chi$ is
its spatial gradient, and $d\mathbf{x}$ is an infinitesimal displacement in
physical space.

This parent name does not by itself specify a norm, component, projection
direction, surface average, or normalization of $\chi$. The [toroidal flux
coordinate gradient
magnitude](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_gradient_magnitude) is a concrete
child that selects the norm of the same underlying gradient; other qualified
children would select other scalar forms.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_current_center
items.description:
Signed vertical position of the plasma-current centroid, obtained by
weighting the toroidal current distribution by height in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical coordinate of the plasma-current center is the
current-density-weighted centroid height of the plasma current distribution
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{c}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{A}} Z\,j_{\phi}(R,Z)\,dA}{\int_{\mathcal{A}} j_{\phi}(R,Z)\,dA}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{c}}$ and $Z$ are vertical coordinates in m, $R$ is major
radius in m, $j_{\phi}$ is toroidal current density in A m$^{-2}$, $dA$ is
differential poloidal cross-sectional area in m$^{2}$, and $\mathcal{A}$ is
the region carrying plasma current. The current-weighted center is distinct
from the geometric axis; its radial counterpart is the [radial coordinate of
the current center](name:radial_coordinate_of_current_center).

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-current centroid lies in the $+Z$
direction from the coordinate origin.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description:
Bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles in one specified
internal quantum or energy state, given by the first moment of their
velocity distribution.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the bulk translational velocity vector of neutral particles
occupying one specified internal state, such as a quantum or energy state.
It retains resolution of that state rather than combining distinct neutral
internal states.

The state-resolved bulk velocity is the first velocity moment of the
corresponding distribution:

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\alpha} = \frac{\int \mathbf{v}\,f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}{\int f_{\alpha}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}}
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\alpha}$ is the bulk velocity, $\alpha$ identifies the
internal state, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{\alpha}$ is the
velocity distribution for that state.

This is the neutral specialization of internal_state_velocity. Unlike
[neutral_velocity](name:neutral_velocity), which may combine or resolve
internal states, this quantity is defined for one specified state. The full
vector is the parent quantity for projections such as
[radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity)
and
[poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when a component points along its corresponding
positive unit vector $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient for field-aligned diffusion of a neutral species'
momentum in one internal state, relating momentum flux to the opposing
flow-velocity gradient.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the kinematic transport coefficient governing diffusive
transport of a neutral species' linear [momentum](name:momentum) along the
local magnetic-field direction, resolved for one specified internal state.
It specializes [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) by
selecting the neutral population, internal state, and transport direction.

In a local flow-gradient closure, the field-aligned diffusive momentum flux
satisfies:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -m_0 n_{0,a} D_{0,a,\parallel}\left(\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla\right)\mathbf u_{0,a}
$$

where the subscript $0$ denotes the neutral species, $a$ identifies its
internal state, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the
vector of momentum components transported diffusively along the magnetic
field, $m_0$ is the neutral-particle mass, $n_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved
number density, $D_{0,a,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity, and $\mathbf
u_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved mean flow velocity. The unit vector
$\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the local magnetic field
$\mathbf B$, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The parallel qualifier selects the transport and velocity-gradient
direction; it does not require that the transported momentum itself be
field-parallel. The coefficient applies to one neutral species and internal
state, without averaging over internal states. Internal-state resolution is
distinct from ion charge-state resolution. Only gradient-driven diffusive
transport is included; convective momentum transport, residual stress, and
momentum sources are separate contributions. A down-gradient closure uses a
nonnegative coefficient.

This is the field-aligned directional member of the [neutral internal-state
momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient),
rather than its complete set of directional coefficients.

items.name: radial_magnetization_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Signed radial component of the effective magnetization vector assigned to a
ferritic element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Radial magnetization of a ferritic element is the projection of its
effective magnetization vector onto the cylindrical major-radius direction.
It describes the element's magnetization, not the radial component of the
surrounding magnetic field.

$$
M_R = \mathbf{M} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $M_R$ is the radial magnetization, $\mathbf{M}$ is the effective
magnetization vector assigned to the ferritic element, and $\hat{R}$ is the
outward radial unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame. The [vertical magnetization of the ferritic
element](name:vertical_magnetization_of_ferritic_element) and [toroidal
magnetization of the ferritic
element](name:toroidal_magnetization_of_ferritic_element) are the
corresponding projections onto the other cylindrical directions. This
quantity is distinct from the [radial magnetic field at the ferritic element
centroid](name:radial_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid), which
describes magnetic flux density rather than magnetization.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective magnetization points toward
increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: vertical_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective vertical convection velocity that advects a chosen component of
ion momentum density for a specified ion species, represented as the
density-weighted mean over all charge states. The vertical label names the
velocity direction, not the transported momentum component.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion momentum convection velocity is the vertical effective
velocity that advects a chosen component of ion momentum density for a
specified ion species. The vertical direction is the $Z$ projection in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the vertical label
names the velocity direction, not the transported momentum component.
Because this is an intensive species-level quantity, it is the
density-weighted mean over all charge states of that species.

The vertical convective flux density of an ion-momentum component is
represented by:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z} = p_{i,a}\,V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}
$$

where $p_{i,a}=n_i m_i u_{i,a}$ is the ion momentum density associated with
ion flow component $u_{i,a}$, $n_i$ is the ion density, $m_i$ is the ion
mass, $a$ labels the momentum component being transported,
$V_{i,\mathrm{mom,conv},Z}$ is the vertical ion momentum convection
velocity, and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{conv}}_{p_{i,a},Z}$ is the corresponding
vertical convective flux density of that momentum component.

This quantity is the convective coefficient multiplying local ion momentum
density; it excludes diffusive viscosity, residual stress, and explicit
momentum sources. It is not generally identical to the bulk [vertical ion
velocity](name:vertical_ion_velocity), because it characterizes transport of
momentum density rather than the mean particle flow. The unprojected
coefficient is [ion momentum convection
velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity); other projections specify
their own directions.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection carries the selected
ion momentum density toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: volume_averaged_helium_3_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the mean charged-ion
population over the confined plasma volume, summed over singly ionized and
fully stripped states and excluding neutral atoms.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged helium-3 ion number density is the spatial mean of the
charged helium-3 ion population throughout the confined plasma volume. It is
derived from the local [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density), rather
than representing a density at one location.

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and
$n_{{}^{3}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion density summed
over singly ionized and fully stripped states. Neutral helium-3 atoms are
excluded. The [line-averaged helium-3
density](name:line_averaged_helium_3_density) instead averages the same
local quantity along a specified path.

items.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the volume-integrated
toroidal linear momentum of the confined plasma inside the pedestal-top flux
surface, summed over electrons and all ion species. It is the pedestal-top
endpoint of total toroidal plasma momentum, not a local momentum density or
toroidal angular momentum.
items.documentation:
Toroidal plasma momentum at the pedestal top is the cumulative toroidal
component of plasma linear momentum contained inside the flux surface
located at the top of the H-mode pedestal, summed over electrons and all ion
species. The toroidal component is taken in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

Let $\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}$ denote the radial flux-surface label of the
pedestal-top flux surface and let $V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})$ be the plasma
volume enclosed by that surface. The quantity is the radial cumulative
[toroidal_total_plasma_momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum)
evaluated at the pedestal-top endpoint:

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{ped}} = P_\phi(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}}) = \int_{V(\rho_{\mathrm{ped}})} \sum_s m_s n_s(\mathbf{x}) v_{\phi,s}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_\phi(\rho)$ is the cumulative toroidal plasma momentum inside the
flux surface labeled by $\rho$, $s$ indexes electrons and all ion species,
$m_s$ is the species particle mass, $n_s$ is the species number density,
$v_{\phi,s}$ is the signed toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{x}$ is
position, and $dV$ is the volume element.

This quantity is an endpoint value of a volume-integrated radial function:
it is not the local toroidal momentum density $\sum_s m_s n_s v_{\phi,s}$ on
the pedestal-top surface, and it is not a flux-surface average. It is also
not toroidal angular momentum; the angular-momentum integral would include
the moment arm $R$ multiplying the toroidal linear-momentum density. The
same cumulative quantity has related endpoint values at the [magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis) and at the plasma
boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net toroidal plasma momentum points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed transfer rate of a
selected linear-momentum component per surface area, attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport.
items.documentation:
Momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of a
selected component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) attributed to
pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport. The direction of the
transported momentum is distinct from the normal direction of the surface
across which it is transferred.

The contribution through an oriented surface is defined by

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_p \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n}
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Pi}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum-flux tensor contribution
attributed to diamagnetic drift, $\hat{\mathbf e}_p$ is the unit vector
selecting the transported momentum component, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the
chosen positive unit normal to the transfer surface. The tensor's first
index denotes the transported momentum direction and its second index
denotes the transport direction.

For the total momentum balance, the contributing population and charge-state
fluxes are summed. No particular species, charge state, momentum axis,
surface orientation, or plasma region is selected by this general quantity.
It is normalized to the actual surface area, not integrated over that area,
and excludes contributions from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms.

The [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and [neutral
momentum flux due to diamagnetic
drift](name:neutral_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) specialize the
participating population. Neutral specializations denote momentum transport
attributed to this mechanism, not a direct magnetic drift of uncharged
particles.

Sign convention: Positive when positive momentum along $\hat{\mathbf e}_p$
is transported through the surface in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf n}$.

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_flux
items.description:
Field-parallel neutral energy flux is the signed thermal-energy transport
per unit area and time along the local magnetic field by one neutral species
in one specified internal state.
items.documentation:
Field-parallel neutral internal-state energy flux describes thermal-energy
transport across a surface perpendicular to the local magnetic field by one
neutral species in one specified internal state. It is the field-aligned
component of the [neutral internal-state energy
flux](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_flux).

The defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,a,W,\parallel} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is the signed field-parallel thermal-energy
flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a,W}$ is the thermal-energy flux vector of the
selected neutral species in internal state $a$, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf
B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf
B$, whose magnitude is $|\mathbf B|$. The subscripts $0$, $W$, and
$\parallel$ identify the neutral population, energy channel, and
field-parallel projection, respectively.

This contribution applies to one internal state, not a sum over states or
species. Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives
the [parallel neutral energy flux](name:parallel_neutral_energy_flux). The
magnetic field defines the projection direction; it does not imply that
neutral particles are constrained to follow magnetic field lines. The
projection requires a nonzero local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when thermal energy carried by the selected
neutral population flows in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: effective_charge_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Effective charge at the magnetic axis is the local charge-squared-weighted
ion charge sum divided by the electron density, evaluated at the magnetic
axis. It equals 1 for a plasma containing only singly charged
hydrogen-isotope ions and increases with impurity charge content.
items.documentation:
Effective charge at the magnetic axis is the local charge-squared-weighted
ion charge sum divided by the electron density, evaluated at the magnetic
axis. It is the on-axis value of [effective charge](name:effective_charge).
It equals unity for a plasma containing only singly charged hydrogen-isotope
ions, and higher-charge impurity ions contribute disproportionately because
the charge number is squared.

For a local ion mixture, the on-axis effective charge is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff,axis}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) Z_s^2}{n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}})}
$$

where $s$ indexes ion species or ionization states present at the
magnetic-axis location, $n_s$ is the corresponding ion number density in
$\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, $Z_s$ is the positive ion charge number, $n_e$ is the
electron number density in $\mathrm{m}^{-3}$, and
$\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ denotes the magnetic-axis location.

The sum includes charged ions and excludes neutral atoms, neutral molecules,
and electrons. For a locally quasineutral plasma, $n_e = \sum_s n_s Z_s$, so
the same quantity may be interpreted as the ion-density-weighted ratio
$\langle Z^2 \rangle / \langle Z \rangle$. This locus-specific value is
distinct from effective charge at the plasma boundary.

items.name: total_fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Gyrotropic pressure tensor of the suprathermal ion population summed over
all charge states, characterized by independent components parallel and
perpendicular to the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The total fast-ion pressure represents the full gyrotropic kinetic stress of
the suprathermal ion population, summed over all charge states, as a
contribution to the plasma pressure balance. Fast ions — including
fusion-born alpha particles, neutral-beam-injected ions, and
radio-frequency-accelerated ions — retain pressure anisotropy with
$P_\parallel \neq P_\perp$ relative to the local magnetic field because
their pitch-angle scattering rate is slow compared with their energy
transfer rate to the bulk plasma. The anisotropic structure is fully
captured by the two independent scalar components [parallel total fast-ion
pressure](name:parallel_total_fast_ion_pressure) and [perpendicular total
fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure).

For a gyrotropic fast-ion distribution, the pressure tensor is:

$$
\overleftrightarrow{P}_\text{fast} = P_{\perp}\,\overleftrightarrow{I} + (P_{\parallel} - P_{\perp})\,\hat{b}\hat{b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel}$ and $P_{\perp}$ are the parallel and perpendicular
scalar pressure components, $\hat{b} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit
vector along the local magnetic field, and $\overleftrightarrow{I}$ is the
identity tensor.

Fast-ion pressure profiles are obtained from kinetic particle-following or
Fokker-Planck solvers that evolve the suprathermal distribution function
under collisional slowing-down and pitch-angle scattering. The anisotropic
fast-ion stress enters the MHD force balance and can drive
pressure-anisotropy-driven instabilities when $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$
departs significantly from unity. The parent quantity
[fast_ion_pressure](name:fast_ion_pressure) provides per-charge-state
resolution.

In high-performance discharges with strong neutral beam or ion cyclotron
resonance heating, fast-ion pressure can reach 10–50% of the total plasma
pressure in the core, with anisotropy ratios $P_{\parallel}/P_{\perp}$
ranging from near unity for isotropized distributions to several for
strongly beam-like distributions.

items.name: energy_flux_at_limiter
items.description:
Plasma energy deposition rate per unit area on the plasma-facing surface of
a limiter, without implying a maximum or other surface aggregation.
items.documentation:
Energy flux at a limiter is the plasma energy deposition rate per unit area
on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. It is a surface power-density
quantity for plasma-wall interaction with the limiter material.

For a surface element on the limiter, the local limiter energy flux $q_E$ is
defined by the deposited plasma power per surface area:

$$
q_E = \frac{dP_\mathrm{dep}}{dA}
$$

where $q_E$ is the energy flux at the limiter, $P_\mathrm{dep}$ is the
plasma power deposited on the limiter surface element, and $A$ is the area
of that surface element.

This parent quantity applies to limiter plasma-facing surfaces and does not
by itself specify a spatial maximum, average, integral, component, or
normalization. It excludes total power deposited on the limiter, which is
obtained by integrating the energy flux over surface area, and it excludes
energy deposition on non-limiter plasma-facing components unless those
components are acting as the limiter surface.

The [maximum energy flux at limiter](name:energy_flux_maximum_at_limiter) is
the surface maximum of this limiter energy-flux quantity over the limiter
plasma-facing surface.

items.name: spectral_calibration_factor_at_line_of_sight
items.description:
Wavelength-specific interferometric conversion coefficient that converts a
signed phase change along a line of sight into electron column density.
items.documentation:
The spectral calibration factor is the wavelength-specific proportionality
that maps an interferometric phase change along one line of sight to the
electron column density on that optical path.

The conversion is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{line}} = K_{\mathrm{spec}}\,\Delta\varphi
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{line}}$ is the [line-integrated electron number
density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density), $K_{\mathrm{spec}}$
is this spectral calibration factor, and $\Delta\varphi$ is the signed
interferometric phase change.

The factor applies to the complete electron-density integral along the
associated line of sight and to its corresponding probing wavelength. It
represents the electron contribution only and is not a local density, a
line-averaged density, or an optical phase itself.

Applying this factor produces the line-integrated electron number density;
dividing that result by the optical chord length gives [line-averaged
electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density). The associated
wavelength is the spectral parameter of the probing electromagnetic wave,
related to [wavelength of wave beam](name:wavelength_of_wave_beam).

items.name: power_at_wall_due_to_ohmic_dissipation
items.description:
Resistive Joule-heating power deposited in conducting wall structures by
induced or halo currents flowing through them.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the rate of irreversible electrical-energy conversion into
heat within conducting wall and vessel structures, caused by currents
flowing through those structures.

For the conducting wall domain, the ohmic power is defined by

$$
P_{\rm wall}^{\rm ohm} = \int_{V_{\rm wall}} \eta\,\lvert\mathbf{J}\rvert^2\,dV
$$

where $P_{\rm wall}^{\rm ohm}$ is the wall ohmic power, $V_{\rm wall}$ is
the conducting wall volume, $\eta$ is the electrical resistivity of the wall
material, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the current-density vector.

The quantity aggregates resistive heating over the conducting wall and
vessel structures as a single deposited power. It includes Joule heating
from induced currents and halo currents, but excludes ohmic dissipation in
the plasma or other conducting domains and excludes wall power deposited
through thermal conduction, radiation, or particle transport without
resistive current dissipation.

This is the wall-locus specialization of [total ohmic-dissipation
power](name:total_power_due_to_ohmic_dissipation), which aggregates
irreversible electrical-energy conversion over the complete applicable
conducting domain rather than only the wall structures. The resistivity
governing the integrand is the [electrical resistivity of wall
material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material).

items.name: total_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Effective Fickian coefficient relating the diffusive flux of total momentum
to its local momentum-density gradient without selecting a directional
component.
items.documentation:
Total momentum diffusivity is the proportionality coefficient between the
diffusive flux of aggregated momentum and the negative local gradient of
aggregated momentum density, following a Fick's-law closure for momentum
transport.

For each resolved transport direction, the componentwise closure is

$$
\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_i}\left(\sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,i}\right)
$$

where $\Gamma_{m,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of total momentum
component $i$, $D_{m,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the corresponding total momentum
diffusivity component, $x_i$ is the spatial coordinate in direction $i$, $s$
indexes the momentum-carrying populations included in the total, $m_s$ is
the particle mass of population $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, and
$v_{s,i}$ is its velocity component in direction $i$.

The total aggregation sums the momentum contributions of all populations and
charge states included in the physical definition rather than selecting one
species, charge state, or process. The quantity remains direction-general
and vector-valued; no single toroidal, radial, parallel, or other projection
is selected at this level.

This quantity is the total-momentum specialization of [momentum
diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity), retaining its Fick's-law transport
meaning while fixing the population aggregation. The [toroidal total
momentum diffusivity](name:toroidal_total_momentum_diffusivity) is the
directional specialization obtained by selecting the toroidal component of
this vector.

items.name: total_momentum_source
items.description:
Directed rate of momentum transfer to or from all included particle
populations, represented as an area-normalized vector source density.
items.documentation:
A momentum source density represents the directed transfer of momentum
caused by physical processes acting on a plasma population or one of its
resolved states. The total quantity retains the vector direction of the net
momentum-transfer rate while aggregating the included particle populations.

The aggregate source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{p} = \sum_s \frac{\mathrm{d}\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}}{\mathrm{d}A\,\mathrm{d}t}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{p}$ is the total momentum source density,
$\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{src},s}$ is the momentum transferred by source
processes to or from population $s$, and $A$ is the surface over which the
source is normalized. The sum includes only the particle populations
specified by the physical scope of the quantity. Directional projections,
such as [radial total momentum source](name:radial_total_momentum_source),
are components of this vector quantity, while [momentum
source](name:momentum_source) provides the broader family context.

items.name: coolant_pressure_at_cooling_circuit_inlet
items.description:
Coolant pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet is the absolute static pressure
of the coolant where it enters a hydraulically defined cooling circuit or
component. It is the coolant-specific inlet pressure boundary and excludes
gage, dynamic, and stagnation pressure.
items.documentation:
Coolant pressure at a cooling-circuit inlet is the absolute static
thermodynamic pressure of the coolant where it enters a hydraulically
defined cooling circuit or component. It denotes the scalar upstream
boundary pressure of the coolant and excludes gage pressure, dynamic
pressure, and stagnation pressure.

For the same hydraulic flow path, the associated static pressure drop is
related to this inlet pressure by:

$$
p_{\mathrm{coolant,in}} = p_{\mathrm{coolant,out}} + \Delta p_{\mathrm{coolant}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{coolant,in}}$ is this inlet absolute static coolant
pressure in pascals, $p_{\mathrm{coolant,out}}$ is the corresponding outlet
absolute static coolant pressure in pascals, and $\Delta
p_{\mathrm{coolant}}$ is the total static pressure drop in pascals, defined
positive when the outlet static pressure is lower than the inlet static
pressure.

This quantity is the coolant-specific specialization of pressure at a
cooling-circuit inlet: when the working fluid is coolant, both names denote
the same inlet absolute static pressure. It is also the
cooling-circuit-inlet value of [coolant pressure](name:coolant_pressure),
and it is distinct from pressure loss, pump head, and mechanical stress in
the surrounding structure.

items.name: deuterium_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Deuterium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of deuterium ions, summed over all charge states, at the
transport-barrier shoulder.
items.documentation:
Deuterium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the
local concentration of deuterium ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode
transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_D = \sum_z n_{D,z}
$$

where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density and $n_{D,z}$ is the number
density of deuterium ions in charge state $z$.

This quantity applies specifically to deuterium ions and is evaluated
locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized
poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is
summed over all deuterium ion charge states and is not a density-weighted
average, line average, or volume average; neutral deuterium and electrons
are excluded.

It is the deuterium-specific component of the species-resolved [density at
the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). The corresponding [electron
density at the pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top)
describes the electron population at the same locus and is not included in
this ion density.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate
items.description:
Inverse relaxation time for collisional and neoclassical damping of
magnetic-field-aligned ordered momentum carried by ions of one specified
species and charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective inverse relaxation time for collisional and
neoclassical damping of ordered [momentum](name:momentum) parallel to the
local magnetic field. It governs relaxation of the selected ion charge
state's parallel flow in core-plasma momentum balance.

The local linear damping contribution is defined by:

$$
\left.\frac{\partial g_{s,\parallel}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{s,\parallel}g_{s,\parallel}
$$

where $g_{s,\parallel}$ is the ordered field-parallel momentum density of
ions of the specified species and charge state, $s$ identifies that
population, $t$ is time, and $\nu_{s,\parallel}$ is this damping rate. The
subscript $\parallel$ denotes the field-aligned component, and the
restriction labeled $\mathrm{damp}$ isolates the damping contribution to the
momentum balance. For a constant rate, this contribution produces
exponential relaxation with a relaxation time equal to the rate's
reciprocal.

The coefficient is charge-state resolved, not summed or averaged over
species or charge states. It describes local relaxation rather than
diffusive or convective momentum transport or an externally applied momentum
source. Collisional relaxation can transfer momentum to other populations
without implying loss of total plasma momentum.

This is the parallel-component specialization of [ion charge-state momentum
damping rate](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate). It differs from
[parallel ion momentum damping
rate](name:parallel_ion_momentum_damping_rate), which describes aggregate
bulk-ion flow rather than the flow of one specified ion charge state.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the
area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It
represents momentum transfer along the local magnetic-field direction.
items.documentation:
Parallel ion charge-state momentum source is the parallel projection of the
area-normalized momentum source acting on one specified ion charge state. It
represents directional momentum transfer to or from that charge state
resolved along the local magnetic-field direction, rather than summed over
charge states.

The parallel projection is defined by projecting the momentum-source vector
for that charge state onto the local magnetic-field unit vector:

$$
S_{\parallel,i,Z} = \mathbf{S}_{i,Z} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{i,Z}$ is the area-normalized momentum-source vector
acting on ion species $i$ in charge state $Z$, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} =
\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is distinct from the [poloidal ion charge-state momentum
source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source) and the [toroidal
ion charge-state momentum
source](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source), which use poloidal
and toroidal projections of the same charge-state-resolved momentum source.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum-source vector acting on the
charge state has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the
local magnetic-field unit vector.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux
items.description:
Poloidal momentum flux for one ion charge state is the net transfer rate of
that state's poloidal linear momentum across a magnetic flux surface,
divided by the surface area.
items.documentation:
Poloidal momentum flux for an ion charge state is the
surface-area-normalized rate at which that state's poloidal linear
[momentum](name:momentum) crosses a magnetic flux surface. The poloidal
label selects the transported momentum component; transport is across the
surface, not along a poloidal arc.

The defining relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{p}} = \frac{\dot{P}_{z,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{out}}}{A}
$$

where $\Gamma_{z,\mathrm{p}}$ is this momentum flux,
$\dot{P}_{z,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the signed net outward transfer
rate of poloidal linear momentum across the entire flux surface, $A$ is that
surface's area, and $z$ identifies the specified ionic charge state. The
subscript $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal component. The positive poloidal
direction is tangent to the surface toward increasing poloidal angle
$\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels flux
surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle.

This quantity includes convective and nonconvective momentum transport,
rather than only its diffusive contribution. It is a flux density, not the
surface-integrated transfer rate or a local momentum source. It applies to
one ionic charge state and is not summed over charge states.

It is the poloidal transported-momentum component of [ion charge-state
momentum flux](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). Summing it over all
ionic charge states of the same species gives the [poloidal ion momentum
flux](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the net transport of positive poloidal
momentum is outward toward the last closed flux surface.

items.name: neutral_momentum_source
items.description:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population,
summed over all neutral internal states, giving the net directed rate of
momentum transfer.
items.documentation:
Area-normalized vector momentum source density for the neutral population is
the net directed rate of momentum transfer to all neutral internal states.

The aggregate source is the sum of the contributions from each resolved
neutral internal state:

$$
\mathbf{S}_{n}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{N}}\mathbf{S}_{n,a}
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{n}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum source density,
$\mathcal{N}$ is the set of neutral internal states, and $\mathbf{S}_{n,a}$
is the [neutral internal-state momentum
source](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_source) for state $a$. It is
the neutral specialization of the general [momentum
source](name:momentum_source), and its projections include the [poloidal
neutral momentum source](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_source) and toroidal
counterpart.

The quantity is summed over neutral internal states and is not a
single-state source. Its vector direction is retained rather than reduced to
a magnitude.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along its
designated positive direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, or along the local magnetic-field direction for a parallel
projection.

items.name: major_length_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Length of the major oblique side of a plasma-filament cross-section,
inclined relative to the major-radius axis and distinct from the
height-oriented side.
items.documentation:
Major length of a plasma filament is the Euclidean length of the oblique
parallelogram side associated with the major-radius direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the side lies in the
poloidal $R$-$Z$ cross-section and is defined by

$$
L_{\mathrm{major}} = \sqrt{(\Delta R)^2 + (\Delta Z)^2}
$$

where $L_{\mathrm{major}}$ is the major oblique-side length, $\Delta R$ is
the difference in major-radius coordinates between the side endpoints, and
$\Delta Z$ is the corresponding difference in vertical coordinates.

This quantity applies to one discrete plasma current-carrying filament
element and describes only its major oblique side. It is an individual
geometric length, not a sum, average, or aggregate over filament elements,
and it excludes the other oblique side represented by the [minor length of a
plasma filament](name:minor_length_of_plasma_filament).

It is the major-qualified component of length of a plasma filament,
selecting the side associated with the major-radius direction rather than
defining an additional length to be added to the parent quantity. Its
inclination is described separately by the [inclination angle of a plasma
filament](name:alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament).

items.name: methane_carbon_13_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma
vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate with 10 equivalent
electrons assigned to each neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous injection rate of carbon-13-labeled methane into the plasma
vessel is the rate at which neutral $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ enters the plasma
vessel, counted using the equivalent-electron convention. Each neutral
carbon-13-labeled methane molecule contributes 10 equivalent electrons.

The constitutive relation between the equivalent-electron source rate and
the molecular injection rate is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4} = 10\,\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the carbon-13-labeled methane source
rate, $\dot{N}_{^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4}$ is the molecule-counted injection rate
