of neutral carbon-13-labeled methane, and $^{13}\mathrm{CH}_4$ denotes
methane with carbon-13 as the carbon isotope.

This quantity applies only to neutral carbon-13-labeled methane crossing
into the plasma vessel by gas injection, aggregated over the relevant
injection locations as an instantaneous total. It excludes unlabeled
methane, other hydrocarbons, gas remaining upstream of the vessel, and
accumulated injected amount.

It is distinguished from a molecule-counted [methane source
rate](name:methane_source_rate) by the equivalent-electron counting
convention: the present quantity is 10 times the corresponding
molecule-counted rate for the same carbon-13-labeled methane population.
When the corresponding accumulated count is used, this source rate is the
time derivative of the [accumulated methane carbon-13 count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_methane_carbon_13_count_due_to_gas_injection)
under the same equivalent-electron convention.

Sign convention: Positive when carbon-13-labeled methane enters the plasma
vessel.

items.name: electron_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Electron temperature averaged along an open magnetic field line between
upstream and downstream locations in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the mean bulk-electron thermal temperature along an open
magnetic field line through the scrape-off layer, between specified upstream
and downstream locations. It represents the connected-field-line average
rather than the local electron temperature at a single position.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_e = \frac{1}{L_{\parallel}} \int_{s_u}^{s_d} T_e(s)\,ds
$$

where $T_e(s)$ is the local electron temperature, $s$ is arc length along
the magnetic field line, $s_u$ and $s_d$ are the upstream and downstream
endpoints, and $L_{\parallel}=s_d-s_u$ is the connection length.

The quantity applies to the bulk electron population in the scrape-off layer
and is aggregated by arc-length averaging along one open field line. It
excludes local single-point temperature values and does not represent a
flux-surface or volume average.

This is the electron-species specialization of the [field-line-averaged
temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer). It is
distinct from the corresponding [ion field-line-averaged
temperature](name:ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer),
which uses the ion temperature, and from [temperature over the scrape-off
layer](name:temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), which averages over the
region rather than along a connected field line.

items.name: toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal component of hydrogen-ion bulk velocity, averaged
over ionization states at the magnetic axis in the right-handed cylindrical
(R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the hydrogen-ion bulk-flow velocity component in the
toroidal direction at the magnetic axis. It includes the hydrogen ion
population across its ionization states and excludes neutral hydrogen.

At the magnetic axis, the charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}} V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}}
$$

where $q$ indexes hydrogen ion charge states, $n_{\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and
$V_{\phi,\mathrm{H}^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. The
magnetic axis is the location where the gradient of the poloidal magnetic
flux vanishes. The component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The same hydrogen-ion quantity at other loci is given by [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_pedestal_top) and [toroidal hydrogen
velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_hydrogen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).
Species-specific counterparts include [toroidal deuterium velocity at the
magnetic axis](name:toroidal_deuterium_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and
[toroidal helium-3 velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

Sign convention: Positive when the hydrogen-ion flow points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: incident_angle_at_wall
items.description:
Incident angle at wall is the angle between the incoming neutral-particle
velocity and the wall-surface normal directed into the material. It is the
species-specific angular coordinate for physical sputtering by neutral
projectiles; zero is normal incidence and grazing incidence approaches a
right angle.
items.documentation:
Incident angle at wall is the geometrical angle between the velocity
direction of an incident neutral particle at impact and the local
wall-surface normal directed from the plasma-facing side into the wall
material. It characterizes the incidence direction of a selected
neutral-particle species on the wall.

The incidence angle $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\alpha = \arccos\left(\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}$ is the unit direction of the incoming
neutral-particle velocity at the impact point and
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}$ is the local wall-surface unit normal
directed into the wall material.

The scope is a specified neutral incident species interacting with the wall.
The allowed interval is $0 \le \alpha \le \pi/2$: $\alpha=0$ corresponds to
normal incidence into the wall, and $\alpha=\pi/2$ corresponds to tangential
grazing incidence. Directions for which the particle is leaving the
wall-facing half-space are not incident angles.

This quantity is the angular argument for the physical sputtering dependence
of that neutral species at the wall. It is not the physical sputtering
coefficient, not an angle for emitted or sputtered particles, and not an
average over neutral species or wall locations.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral
nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that
location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states. It represents
nitrogen ions specifically, rather than neutral nitrogen, electrons, or
other ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{N,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{N,ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N,axis}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{N,ion}}$ is the total number of nitrogen ions
summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete nitrogen-ion population at that
location, uses a sum over nitrogen ionic charge states, and excludes neutral
nitrogen; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of
another species.

This is the nitrogen-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It follows
the same charge-state-summed convention as [helium-4 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis), while differing in the ion
species counted.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Poloidal projection of the gage-dependent magnetic vector potential along
the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates (psi,
θ, φ).
items.documentation:
The poloidal component $A_\theta$ is the projection of the [magnetic vector
potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) $\mathbf{A}$ onto the unit
tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux
coordinates $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$. It is a signed, gage-dependent component
of the electromagnetic potential.

The defining projection is:

$$
A_\theta(\psi,\theta,\phi)=\mathbf{A}(\psi,\theta,\phi)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta
$$

where $\mathbf{A}$ is the magnetic vector potential,
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing $\theta$,
$\psi$ is the flux label, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The full
potential satisfies $\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}$, where $\mathbf{B}$
is the magnetic induction.

Only the curl of $\mathbf{A}$ is gage invariant, so this component depends
on the chosen gage. Unlike the [parallel magnetic vector
potential](name:parallel_magnetic_vector_potential), it projects onto the
flux-coordinate poloidal tangent rather than the magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{A}$ points along
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta$, toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: toroidal_impurity_ion_velocity_at_measurement_position
items.description:
Toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of an impurity-ion population,
evaluated at a specified measurement position.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the
toroidal direction at the specified measurement position. It is a signed
velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
v_\phi(\mathbf{x}_m)=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{imp}}(\mathbf{x}_m)\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{x}_m$ is the
measurement position, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the bulk velocity of
the impurity-ion population, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

For an impurity population combined over charge states, the bulk velocity is
the density-weighted mean over the included charge states. The species and
charge-state aggregation must be interpreted from the defined population;
the related [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity) provides the
corresponding generic ion quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the impurity-ion flow points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: total_thermal_power_at_outlet
items.description:
Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal
energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet
streams. It includes all rejected heat contributions and excludes useful
electrical output.
items.documentation:
Total thermal power at the outlet is the aggregate rate at which thermal
energy leaves a power-conversion cycle through all heat-rejection outlet
streams. It represents the total rejected heat load delivered from the
conversion cycle to its heat sink, excluding useful electrical output.

The total outlet thermal power is the sum of the thermal-power contributions
from the individual heat-rejection outlet streams:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{O}} P_{\mathrm{th,out},i} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{waste,out}}}{dt}
$$

where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of heat-rejection outlet streams,
$P_{\mathrm{th,out},i}$ is the thermal power carried by outlet stream $i$,
$E_{\mathrm{waste,out}}$ is the cumulative rejected thermal energy in J, and
$t$ is time in s.

This quantity is the aggregate over outlet streams; an individual
outlet-stream contribution is thermal_power_at_outlet. For a steady
conversion cycle with no net energy accumulation inside the conversion
boundary, it is related to total_thermal_power_at_inlet by the first-law
balance $P_{\mathrm{th,out}}^{\mathrm{tot}} =
P_{\mathrm{th,in}}^{\mathrm{tot}} - P_{\mathrm{net}}$, where
$P_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the net useful electrical power delivered by the
conversion system.

items.name: particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven
items.description:
Distribution-function-driven particle source rate is the net particle gain
or loss per physical volume and time from a kinetic source acting on a
specified population.
items.documentation:
Distribution-function-driven particle source rate is the net volumetric
particle production or removal contributed by a source acting on a specified
population's kinetic distribution. It is the contribution of that source to
the particle continuity equation.

The rate is the zeroth velocity moment of the kinetic source term:

$$
S(\mathbf{x},t) = \int Q(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $S$ is the volumetric particle source rate, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial
position, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $Q$ is the kinetic
particle source density per velocity-space volume, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full velocity space
of the specified population.

The quantity includes particle gains and losses from the specified source,
not a total over unrelated source mechanisms. It does not impose a
particular species, charge state, or thermal-population restriction. It is
distinct from the velocity-space-resolved source density and from density
changes caused by transport-flux divergence.

No spatial averaging or volume integration is implied. Integrating this
quantity over a specified physical volume gives the corresponding
[volume-integrated particle source
rate](name:volume_integrated_particle_source_rate).

Sign convention: Positive when the specified source adds particles to the
population; negative when it removes them.

items.name: perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description:
Local kinetic stress per degree of freedom perpendicular to the magnetic
field, carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose
orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current; its
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of this local quantity over a
magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the mean of the two
kinetic-stress components perpendicular to the local magnetic field, carried
by suprathermal particles on counter-passing orbits. These are untrapped
orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current.

For a species $s$, the local perpendicular pressure is the transverse second
moment of its fast-particle distribution restricted to counter-passing
trajectories:

$$
p_{perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{m_s}{2}\int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})} v_\perp^2 f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is the perpendicular counter-passing
fast-particle pressure, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $m_s$ is its
particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity,
and $v_\perp$ is the magnitude of its component perpendicular to the local
magnetic field. The function $f_s^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the distribution
function of that species' suprathermal particles, and
$\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset
corresponding to counter-passing trajectories at $\mathbf{x}$. The element
$d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The factor one-half averages
the stresses in the two perpendicular directions; the moment retains
directed-motion contributions rather than subtracting the population's mean
velocity.

The quantity applies to suprathermal particles in the counter-passing
population and excludes thermal particles, trapped particles, co-passing
particles, and the field-parallel stress. It is defined locally; its
flux-surface-averaged form is the average of the local pressure over a
magnetic flux surface. When a total over fast-particle species is
represented, the species contributions are added directly.

For the same counter-passing population, the [counter-passing fast-particle
pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), which is one-third
of the kinetic-stress trace, satisfies
$p_s^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}})/3$.
Here $p_s^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is that scalar trace pressure,
$p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is the [parallel counter-passing
fast-particle
pressure](name:parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), and
$p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{fast,cp}}$ is this perpendicular component. Thus this
quantity is neither the sum of the two perpendicular stresses nor the full
scalar trace pressure.

items.name: parallel_mach_number
items.description:
Signed ratio of the plasma flow component along the local magnetic-field
direction to the local plasma sound speed.
items.documentation:
The parallel Mach number is the signed field-aligned flow speed normalized
by the local sound speed. It is the parallel component of the [Mach-number
vector](name:mach_number), rather than the magnitude of the full flow Mach
number.

$$
M_\parallel = \frac{v_\parallel}{c_s}, \qquad v_\parallel = \mathbf{v} \cdot \mathbf{b}
$$

where $M_\parallel$ is the parallel Mach number, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma
flow velocity, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector in the local magnetic-field
direction, $v_\parallel$ is the field-aligned flow component, and $c_s$ is
the local plasma sound speed. The quantity excludes perpendicular flow
contributions and is distinct from the magnitude of the full Mach-number
vector.

items.name: line_averaged_xenon_density
items.description:
Number density of xenon ions averaged along a chord through the plasma,
summed over all ionization states from singly ionized through fully stripped
xenon and excluding neutral xenon atoms.
items.documentation:
The line-averaged xenon ion number density is the chord-length mean of the
local [xenon density](name:xenon_density), which sums xenon ions from singly
ionized through fully stripped xenon and excludes neutral xenon atoms. It
represents the xenon ion content sampled by a specified chord, not the local
value at any single point unless the local density is uniform along that
chord.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{C}} n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)\, d\ell
$$

where $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{Xe},L}$ is the line-averaged xenon ion number
density, $\mathcal{C}$ is the chord segment over which the average is
defined, $L = \int_{\mathcal{C}} d\ell$ is its path length, $\ell$ is
distance along the chord, and $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)$ is the local [xenon
density](name:xenon_density) evaluated on the chord.

The species aggregation is performed over charge states before the line
average: $n_\mathrm{Xe}(\ell)=\sum_{z=1}^{54} n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}(\ell)$,
where $z$ is the xenon ionic charge-state index, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}^{z+}}$ is
the partial density of xenon ions carrying charge $ze$, and $e$ is the
elementary charge. The physical population is charged xenon ions located on
the chord segment through the plasma; neutral xenon atoms and
charge-state-resolved xenon densities are excluded.

This quantity differs from [volume-averaged xenon
density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which averages the same local
xenon density over the plasma volume, and from [xenon density at magnetic
axis](name:xenon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which evaluates it at the
magnetic-axis locus. It is the xenon counterpart of [line-averaged argon
density](name:line_averaged_argon_density) under the same chord-mean
convention.

items.name: volume_averaged_nitrogen_density
items.description:
Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of nitrogen
nuclei number density, with neutral and all ionized charge states included.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged nitrogen density is the plasma-volume mean of the local
number density of nitrogen atomic nuclei. It is a species-level density, so
neutral nitrogen and every ionized charge state contribute to the average;
the local quantity is [nitrogen density](name:nitrogen_density).

The volume average and charge-state aggregation are defined by

$$
\overline{n}_N = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} n_N(\mathbf{r})\,dV, \qquad n_N(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{z=0}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\overline{n}_N$ and $n_{\mathrm{N}^{z+}}$ are number densities in
m$^{-3}$, $V_p$ is the plasma volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{r}$
is position, and $z$ is the nitrogen charge-state index from neutral
nitrogen ($z=0$) through fully stripped nitrogen ($z=7$).

The average is over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux
surface. Unlike [line-averaged nitrogen
density](name:line_averaged_nitrogen_density), it weights volume elements
rather than points along a specified chord.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
Toroidal-angle coordinate of the geometric center of an electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity locates the geometric center used to define the
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror surface in the toroidal direction. For a
spherical mirror, the reference point is the sphere center.

The toroidal angle is defined from the center coordinates in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis:

$$
\phi_{\rm mir} = \operatorname{atan2}(y_{\rm mir}, x_{\rm mir})
$$

where $x_{\rm mir}$ and $y_{\rm mir}$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the
mirror center, with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$ and the zero-angle direction fixed by
the facility convention. This is the device-centered counterpart of the
toroidal coordinate used for a
[reflector](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_reflector).

The coordinate describes the mirror geometry in its reference position and
does not represent the mirror steering angle or the toroidal location of the
launched beam.

Sign convention: Positive when the mirror center lies at increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: back_surface_distance_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Geometric rear-surface clearance between an ion-cyclotron heating antenna
strap and the conducting wall or conductor behind it.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric standoff between the rear surface of an
ion-cyclotron heating antenna strap and the conducting wall or other
conductor located behind that surface.

The clearance is the shortest separation between the two relevant surfaces:

$$
d_{back} = \min_{\mathbf{r}_b \in S_b,\,\mathbf{r}_c \in S_c} \left\|\mathbf{r}_c - \mathbf{r}_b\right\|
$$

where $d_{\rm back}$ is the rear-surface clearance, $S_b$ is the strap back
surface, $S_c$ is the facing conducting-wall or conductor surface, and
$\mathbf{r}_b$ and $\mathbf{r}_c$ are position vectors on those surfaces.

The quantity applies only to the rear-facing separation of the antenna strap
and does not denote the strap thickness, the distance to its inner or outer
cylindrical boundaries, or either oblique cross-sectional length. The
related [inner radius of the antenna
strap](name:inner_radius_of_antenna_strap), [outer radius of the antenna
strap](name:outer_radius_of_antenna_strap), [major length of the antenna
strap](name:major_length_of_antenna_strap), and [minor length of the antenna
strap](name:minor_length_of_antenna_strap) describe other strap dimensions
rather than this conductor clearance.

This geometric clearance is an antenna-design parameter that influences the
strap's loading resistance and radio-frequency coupling efficiency to the
plasma; it is not itself an electrical resistance, coupling coefficient, or
power quantity.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of the neutral beam injector center, measured from
the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a neutral beam injector is the major-radius
location of the injector unit center relative to the toroidal symmetry axis.
It is a nonnegative geometric coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle,
and $Z$ is vertical height.

For the injector center, the radial coordinate is related to its Cartesian
coordinates by

$$
R = \\sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal Cartesian coordinates of the same
injector center in the right-handed Cartesian $(\\hat{x},\\hat{y},\\hat{z})$
basis.

This quantity applies to one selected neutral beam injector unit and
represents the unit-center position only. It is not an aggregate over
multiple injectors and does not represent a beam trajectory, launch point,
deposition location, or plasma response.

It is the neutral-beam-injector specialization of the general [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), with the geometric point fixed to the
injector unit center.

items.name: toroidal_total_runaway_electron_current
items.description:
Total toroidal runaway-electron current is the signed charge-flow rate
carried by the entire runaway-electron population through the full poloidal
plasma cross-section.
items.documentation:
Total toroidal runaway-electron current is the net conventional electric
current carried by runaway electrons through the full poloidal plasma
cross-section. It is the toroidal component of [total runaway-electron
current](name:total_runaway_electron_current).

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{pol}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}} \cdot \hat{\phi}\, dS
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{RE},\phi}$ is the total toroidal runaway-electron current,
$S_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the full plasma cross-section at fixed toroidal angle,
$dS$ is its area element, and $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the
[runaway-electron current density](name:runaway_electron_current_density).
The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The integral includes the entire runaway-electron population and retains
cancelation between oppositely directed current contributions.
Thermal-electron and ion currents are excluded. This is conventional charge
current, not an unsigned particle rate; because electrons carry negative
charge, its direction is opposite their net toroidal motion. The geometric
toroidal projection is distinct from the field-aligned projection
represented locally by [parallel runaway-electron current
density](name:parallel_runaway_electron_current_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the runaway-electron conventional current
flows toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed
from above the positive $Z$ axis.

items.name: radial_total_thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective radial coefficient for diffusive transport of total thermal energy
carried by the ion population in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective diffusivity for radial transport of total ion
thermal energy. “Total” denotes the sum over the included ion species, while
the thermal scope distinguishes energy transport from particle and momentum
transport.

The diffusive radial energy flux is related to the radial gradient of total
ion energy density by:

$$
q_{i,E,R}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,E,R}\frac{\partial w_{i,E}}{\partial R}
$$

where $q_{i,E,R}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive flux of ion
energy, $D_{i,E,R}$ is this radial energy diffusion coefficient, $w_{i,E}$
is total ion energy density, and $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The coefficient describes the diffusive contribution only; it excludes
advective transport represented by the [radial ion-state energy convection
velocity](name:radial_ion_state_energy_convection_velocity). Its directional
role parallels that of the [radial momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), while its
transported quantity is ion energy.

items.name: gyrocenter_frequency
items.description:
Angular velocity vector of a charged-particle gyrocenter orbit in a
magnetized plasma, with toroidal and poloidal components giving the rates of
gyrocenter advance in their respective angular coordinates.
items.documentation:
The gyrocenter frequency vector characterizes how rapidly a charged
particle's guiding center advances angularly in the confining magnetic
geometry, after averaging over the fast cyclotron gyration to isolate the
slower drift and bounce or transit dynamics relevant to transport and
stability.

The vector decomposes into two principal angular components. The [toroidal
gyrocenter frequency](name:toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency) $\dot{\phi}_{gc} =
d\phi_{gc}/dt$ is the rate of change of the gyrocenter toroidal angle $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major
radius and $Z$ is the vertical height. The [poloidal gyrocenter
frequency](name:poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency) $\dot{\theta}_{gc} =
d\theta_{gc}/dt$ is the rate of advance in poloidal angle $\theta$ as
measured in flux coordinates $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a
radial flux-surface label. The two components have qualitatively different
characters: passing particles circulate continuously in the poloidal
direction, while trapped particles bounce and primarily precess toroidally.

These frequencies are computed in gyrokinetic codes from the guiding-center
orbit equations derived from the gyrocenter Hamiltonian, and may be averaged
over the particle distribution function to yield population-representative
angular velocities. They enter directly into the calculation of resonance
conditions for wave-particle interactions and neoclassical transport
coefficients.

Sign convention: Positive toroidal component when the gyrocenter advances in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; positive poloidal
component when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of
a multicomponent plasma, equal to total momentum density divided by total
mass density. It is the single-fluid bulk plasma velocity whose projections
define the radial, poloidal, toroidal, and field-parallel center-of-mass
velocity components.
items.documentation:
Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of
a multicomponent plasma. It is the velocity whose product with total mass
density equals the total plasma momentum density of the species included in
the plasma mixture.

The center-of-mass velocity $\mathbf{V}_{cm}$ is defined as total momentum
density divided by total mass density:

$$
\mathbf{V}_{cm} = \frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s m_s n_s} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\rho}
$$

where $s$ indexes included plasma species, $m_s$ is the particle mass of
species $s$, $n_s$ is the number density of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is
the species fluid velocity entering the [plasma
velocity](name:plasma_velocity) aggregate, $\rho_s=m_s n_s$ is the species
contribution to mass density, and $\rho=\sum_s \rho_s$ is the total mass
density.

The weighting is by mass density, not by charge, number density alone, or an
unweighted species average. When [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity)
denotes the single-fluid bulk velocity of the same mixture, it is identical
to center-of-mass velocity. Projections of this vector define the
[radial](name:radial_center_of_mass_velocity),
[poloidal](name:poloidal_bulk_center_of_mass_velocity),
[toroidal](name:toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity), and
[field-parallel](name:parallel_center_of_mass_velocity) center-of-mass
velocity components.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_flux
items.description:
Toroidal neutral momentum flux measures signed toroidal linear-momentum
transfer per unit area and time across an oriented surface in the edge
plasma, summed over neutral species and internal states.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neutral momentum flux describes the transfer of the toroidal
component of [linear momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface by
neutral atoms and molecules in the edge plasma. It is the toroidal
projection of the [neutral momentum flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux).

For a surface with a chosen orientation, this component is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_\phi^0 = \hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^0(\hat{\mathbf n})
$$

where $\Gamma_\phi^0$ is the toroidal neutral momentum flux,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^0(\hat{\mathbf n})$ is the vector of neutral linear
momentum transferred per unit area and time across the surface, and
$\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface unit normal. The superscript $0$
denotes the neutral population. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points along
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The flux includes convective transport and isotropic neutral-pressure
contributions, summed over all neutral species and internal states; ion and
electron contributions are excluded. The [internal-state-resolved
counterpart](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) instead
restricts the neutral population to one specified internal state.

The toroidal qualifier selects the transported momentum component, not the
surface-normal direction: the surface normal need not be toroidal. This
quantity is a flux of linear momentum, not angular momentum.

Sign convention: Positive when the net neutral momentum transferred across
the surface, counted in the chosen normal orientation, has a positive
projection along increasing toroidal angle.

items.name: beryllium_density
items.description:
Local number density of beryllium impurity ions per unit plasma volume,
summed over all ionization states from singly ionized to fully stripped
(Be1+ through Be4+), excluding neutral beryllium atoms.
items.documentation:
Beryllium (atomic number $Z = 4$) enters the plasma primarily through
sputtering or evaporation from beryllium first-wall surfaces. The local
beryllium ion number density $n_\mathrm{Be}$ aggregates contributions from
all four charged ionization stages:

$$
n_\mathrm{Be} = \sum_{z=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}^{z+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions in
charge state $z+$, with $z$ running from 1 (singly ionized) to 4 (fully
stripped). Neutral beryllium atoms are excluded from this sum.

Beryllium impurity content is inferred from passive spectroscopy of
beryllium emission lines or from active charge-exchange recombination
spectroscopy, with spatially resolved profiles reconstructed by tomographic
inversion of chord-integrated measurements. Spatially averaged
representations include
[line_averaged_beryllium_density](name:line_averaged_beryllium_density)
along a diagnostic chord and
[volume_averaged_beryllium_density](name:volume_averaged_beryllium_density)
integrated over the confined plasma volume. The relative impurity abundance
with respect to the electron population is characterized by the
ratio_of_beryllium_density_to_electron_density.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of a specified point of a ferritic element, equal to
its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of ferritic element

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $x$ and $y$ are horizontal position coordinates,
and $z$ is vertical position in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ frame
with its origin on the toroidal symmetry axis.

For thick-line geometry, the specified point is the first or second
endpoint, with each coordinate referring to one endpoint separately. For
oblique geometry, it is the designated geometric point. The coordinate is
not an average over the element and does not imply its centroid.

items.name: electron_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population,
representing angular-momentum exchange with other plasma populations for
both fast and thermal electrons.
items.documentation:
Collisionally transferred net torque on the electron population is the
volume-integrated rate of angular-momentum transfer caused by Coulomb
collisions with other plasma populations. It is the electron-specific member
of the broader [torque due to collisions](name:torque_due_to_collisions)
family and parallels [fast torque due to
collisions](name:fast_torque_due_to_collisions).

The defining relation is

$$
\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{dL_{e,\mathrm{coll}}}{dt}
$$

where $\tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the net collisional torque on the electron
population, $L_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ is its volume-integrated angular momentum
transferred by collisions, and $t$ is time.

This parent covers both fast and thermal electron cases, represented by
fast-electron torque due to collisions and [thermal-electron torque due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_due_to_collisions). It excludes
torque on ions, which belongs to [ion torque due to
collisions](name:ion_torque_due_to_collisions), and excludes non-collisional
torque mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions increase the electron population's
angular momentum in the positive rotational sense about the torque axis.

items.name: toroidal_tungsten_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Density-weighted mean toroidal velocity of tungsten impurity ions at the
H-mode pedestal top, averaged over all tungsten ion charge states.
items.documentation:
The toroidal tungsten velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the
density-weighted mean of the toroidal fluid velocities of tungsten impurity
ions over their ionization states. It is evaluated at the core-side shoulder
of the edge transport barrier in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

The defining charge-state average is

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}} = \frac{\sum_q n_q v_{\phi,q}}{\sum_q n_q}
$$

where $V_{\phi,\mathrm{W}}$ is the tungsten toroidal velocity, $n_q$ is the
number density of tungsten ions in charge state $q$, and $v_{\phi,q}$ is
their toroidal velocity component.

The average is density-weighted over tungsten ion charge states, not a sum
of velocities and not a flux-surface average. It therefore differs from the
toroidal flux-surface-averaged tungsten velocity at the plasma boundary;
[toroidal carbon velocity at the pedestal
top](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top) is the analogous
species-specific quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the tungsten velocity component points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: accumulated_argon_count
items.description:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of
argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each argon
atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons, equal to its atomic number; this
is delivered inventory, not plasma electron content or ionization state.
items.documentation:
Accumulated argon count is the cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of
argon atoms delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown. Each
delivered argon atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ equivalent electrons,
equal to the atomic number of argon.

The accumulated count is defined by integrating the delivered argon atom
injection rate from the plasma-breakdown time:

$$
N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t')\,dt', \qquad Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Ar,eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron argon
count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate in atoms per
second, $t$ is time in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time in seconds.

This quantity includes only argon delivered after breakdown. Argon
introduced before breakdown belongs to the pre-breakdown inventory
represented by argon_count; the accumulated value is not a measure of free
electrons, plasma argon content, retained argon, or argon ionization state,
and is not reduced by subsequent pumping, exhaust, wall retention,
ionization, radiation, or redistribution.
